items.meaning: to lower to a weaker grade
items.example: The bank downgraded the rating.
items.exampleCN: 银行下调了评级。

items.example: The laptop is easily upgradable.
items.exampleCN: 这台笔记本电脑很容易升级。

items.example: Retrograde uses the same gradus root.
items.exampleCN: retrograde 使用同一个 gradus 词根。

items.example: Gradual is built on steps of the same kind.
items.exampleCN: gradual 同样建立在「台阶」的意象上。

items.meaning: a person who has finished a course
items.example: Graduate takes a step up through study.
items.exampleCN: graduate 指通过学习向上迈进的人。

items.example: The suffix -able forms upgradable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 upgradable。

definition_zh: 剧变；动荡；隆起；抬起
definition_en: a big change that causes a lot of worry and trouble, or the act of lifting something upward by force, especially the rising of part of the earth surface
core_image: 地壳被顶起，整片地面向上翻起一道大波
scene: 公司被收购后，每个部门都要重新改组。The takeover brought a period of upheaval to every department in the firm.
sceneCN: 这里 upheaval 取的是「剧变、动荡」（第 1 个义项：引起不安与混乱的大变动）；句意：这次收购给公司每个部门带来了一段动荡时期。

pos.zh: 剧变；动荡；动乱
隆起；抬起（地质上的上升）

derivatives.zh: 原为「用力举起」，是 upheaval 的词根动词
举；抛；起伏
up- 加 heave 构成的旧式动词，义为「向上举起」
起伏的；涌动不停的

senses.title: A violent change in a society or system
senses.definition: a great and sudden change in a social, political, or economic order, usually causing anxiety and disorder
senses.definitionCN: 社会、政治或经济秩序中突然而剧烈的变动，往往带来不安与混乱
senses.example: The reforms set off a decade of social upheaval.
senses.exampleCN: 这些改革引发了长达十年的社会动荡。
senses.why: Upheaval is the noun of upheave, to heave up; the ground being thrown up is exactly what a shaken order feels like.
senses.whyCN: upheaval 来自动词 upheave（向上翻起），地面被掀起来的画面，正是秩序被撼动时的感受。

senses.title: A personal or emotional disturbance
senses.definition: a major disruption in a person life, such as moving, job loss, or loss of a loved one
senses.definitionCN: 个人生活中的重大变动，如搬迁、失业或失去亲人
senses.example: Moving abroad was a huge upheaval for the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 举家搬到国外对全家人来说是巨大的变故。
senses.why: The same outward lifting applies to a private life: routines are lifted out of their place and left upside down.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「被抬离原位」也可以落在个人生活上：日常秩序被整个掀翻。

senses.title: The rising of part of the earth surface
senses.definition: the upward movement of rock layers or land during geological change
senses.definitionCN: 地质变化过程中岩层或陆地的向上运动
senses.example: The upheaval of the crust formed these high ridges.
senses.exampleCN: 地壳的隆起形成了这些高高的山脊。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most literal sense: heave up names the upward push of the ground itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最字面的义项：heave up 本就指地面被向上顶起。

senses.title: The act of lifting something up by force
senses.definition: the action of heaving an object or mass upward, often with effort
senses.definitionCN: 用力把物体或大块物质向上抬起的动作
senses.example: The upheaval of the boulder took four strong men.
senses.exampleCN: 抬起那块巨石动用了四个壮汉。
senses.why: Upheave simply means to heave up, so the word can still name the physical lifting action.
senses.whyCN: upheave 的字面意思就是「向上抛起」，所以这个词仍可指实打实的举起动作。

senses.title: A heavy confused movement of a crowd
senses.definition: a restless or turbulent moving about of many people or things
senses.definitionCN: 众多人或物不安地翻动、涌动
senses.example: An upheaval of the crowd followed the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 宣布之后人群一阵骚动。
senses.why: A sea of people can also heave; the crowd surges up and churns like the ground being pushed.
senses.whyCN: 人海也会 heave（涌动）：人群向上翻腾，与地面被顶起的画面相通。

intro.en: Upheaval is the English noun from upheave, built from the adverb up and the verb heave, which goes back to a Germanic root meaning to lift.
intro.cn: upheaval 是 upheave 的名词形式，由 up（向上）加 heave（举起）构成，heave 上溯到日耳曼语中表示「举起」的词根。

items.en: The verb is built on a Germanic root that means to lift or heave, with a reconstructed form often given as hefjan.
items.cn: 该动词建在日耳曼语表示「举起、抬起」的词根上，重构形式常写作 hefjan。

items.en: The verb hebban or hebban appears early, and the noun hebba refers to a lifting or heaving.
items.cn: 古英语早期就有动词 hebban，名词 hebba 指举起或抛起。

items.en: The spelling settles as heven and then heave, keeping the sense of lifting with effort.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写先作 heven，再定型为 heave，词义仍是用力举起。

items.en: Compound verbs such as upheave join up with heave, and the noun upheaval grows from such forms.
items.cn: upheave 这类「up 加 heave」的复合动词出现，名词 upheaval 由此派生。

items.en: By the nineteenth century upheaval shifts from geological lifting to political and social turmoil.
items.cn: 到了十九世纪，upheaval 由地质上的隆起转指政治与社会的动荡。

note.en: Upheaval belongs to the heave family and stands with disorder words such as turmoil and unrest.
note.cn: upheaval 属于 heave 词族，并与 turmoil、unrest 等表混乱的词相邻。

entries.definition: to lift or pull something heavy with effort
to lift or force something upward
rising and falling heavily
a state of great confusion or disorder
a feeling of anger or dissatisfaction among people
a violent and sudden change or disaster

normalIntro.en: Split the word as up plus heave plus al: a heaving upward, then frozen into a noun of change.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 up 加 heave 加 al：先向上翻起，再固化成表示变动的名词。

normal.en: Heave means to lift something heavy, as in heave a box onto a truck.
normal.cn: heave 表示举起重物，比如把箱子抛上卡车。

normal.en: Up in front tells you the direction: the whole thing is forced upward.
normal.cn: 前面的 up 给出方向：整个东西被向上顶起。

normal.en: The suffix -al turns the verb into a noun, so upheaval is the lifting and also the state that follows.
normal.cn: 后缀 -al 把动词变名词，所以 upheaval 既指抬起这个动作，也指其后留下的状态。

normal.en: Remember the family: heave, upheave, upheaval, heaving.
normal.cn: 记住这个词族：heave、upheave、upheaval、heaving。

normal.en: Collocation memory: political upheaval, social upheaval, economic upheaval all describe shaken orders.
normal.cn: 搭配记忆：political upheaval、social upheaval、economic upheaval 都指被撼动的秩序。

abstract.en: Picture a newspaper front page cracking upward like a sheet of ice.
abstract.cn: 想象报纸头版像冰面一样向上裂开、翘起。

abstract.en: Imagine the floor of your room tilting and everything sliding to one side.
abstract.cn: 想象房间地面倾斜，所有东西都滑向一边。

abstract.en: Think of hands pressed under a heavy table, pushing the whole mass upward.
abstract.cn: 想象双手托在沉重的桌子底下，把整块重物向上顶起。

examples.en: The war caused enormous economic upheaval across the region.
examples.cn: 战争在整个地区造成了巨大的经济动荡。

examples.en: Every upheaval in his life taught him to start over.
examples.cn: 他人生中的每一次剧变都教会他重新开始。

examples.en: Geologists study the slow upheaval that raised these mountains.
examples.cn: 地质学家研究抬升起这些山脉的缓慢隆起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆西风」——西风把阿婆的菜摊整个掀翻，一片动荡；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hebban / hebba（举起）→ 中古英语 heven、heave → 英语 upheave（向上举起）→ upheaval（向上翻起；剧变）。前缀 up 给出方向，核心义是「被抬离原位」。

sensesIntro.en: Upheaval starts as a physical lifting, moves to the rising of the land, and then to any shaken order, from a whole society to one person life.
sensesIntro.cn: upheaval 从实物的「向上举起」出发，转到地壳隆起，再扩到任何被撼动的秩序，从整个社会直到个人生活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the ground itself heaved up in one huge lift.
core.cn: 核心意象：地面被一股大力整体顶起。

branches.en: A shaken social order is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 被撼动的社会秩序是主要的现代义项。

branches.en: A private life turned upside down is the personal sense.
branches.cn: 个人生活被整个掀翻，是个人层面的义项。

branches.en: Geological rising and plain lifting keep the literal sense alive.
branches.cn: 地质隆起与普通抬起保留了字面义。

branches.en: A churning crowd shows the heaving image applied to people.
branches.cn: 翻腾的人群把「涌动」意象用到人身上。

branches.en: Both the social shock and the mountain uplift are an upward force breaking a surface.
branches.cn: 社会冲击与山脉抬升都是向上之力顶破原有表面。

intro.en: Upheaval is a two-part build: the adverb up and the verb heave, with the noun suffix -al on the end.
intro.cn: upheaval 由三部分组成：副词 up、动词 heave，以及句尾的名词后缀 -al。

latinIntro.en: Upheaval has no Latin root; it is native English and Germanic, so no Latin family words are listed.
latinIntro.cn: upheaval 没有拉丁词根，它属于本族英语与日耳曼语来源，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.example: Up- adds the direction of rising.
items.exampleCN: up- 加上「上升」的方向。

items.meaning: to lift or pull with effort
items.example: Heave is the core of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: heave 是整个词族的核心。

items.meaning: forms a noun of action or result
items.meaningCN: 构成表示动作或结果的名词
items.example: The suffix -al makes a noun from the verb upheave.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 把动词 upheave 变成名词。

items.example: Upheave joins the two parts into one verb.
items.exampleCN: upheave 把两部分合成一个动词。

items.example: Upheaval is the noun used for social shock.
items.exampleCN: upheaval 是表示社会冲击的名词。

items.example: The plural counts separate shocks.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式用来数一场场冲击。

items.example: The participle describes a heaving sea.
items.exampleCN: 分词形式形容起伏的海面。

items.example: The past participle keeps the literal sense.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词保留字面义。

items.example: The prefix un- reverses the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 使词义反转。

definition_zh: 上坡的；向山上；艰难的；费力的
definition_en: going or sloping toward a higher place, or difficult and requiring a lot of effort
core_image: 一个人弓着背，推着车沿坡往上爬
scene: 骑行者把档位调到最低，才蹬得动这段长坡。It was an uphill ride that left the cyclists out of breath.
sceneCN: 这里 uphill 是「上坡的、向山上的」（第 1 个义项：朝高处延伸的）；句意：那是一段上坡路，骑得人上气不接下气。

pos.zh: 上坡的；向山上的；艰难的
往山上；上坡地

derivatives.zh: 山丘；up- 加 hill 构成的词，词根就是这个名词
下坡的；下行的，与 uphill 构成方向对照
多小山的，由 hill 加 -y 构成
山坡，由 hill 加 side 组合而成

senses.title: Sloping upward, leading to a higher place
senses.definition: rising toward a higher level, said of a road, path, or piece of ground
senses.definitionCN: 朝更高处倾斜的，用于形容道路、小径或地面
senses.example: The last stretch is a steep uphill road.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一段是陡峭的上坡路。
senses.why: Up tells the direction and hill the place, so uphill names ground that climbs.
senses.whyCN: up 给出方向，hill 给出地点，所以 uphill 本义就是「往上通向山丘的地面」。

senses.title: Toward a higher point, as an adverb of direction
senses.definition: in an upward direction along a slope, used to describe movement or position
senses.definitionCN: 沿斜坡朝上的方向，用于描述动作或位置
senses.example: We walked uphill for nearly an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 我们向上走了将近一个小时。
senses.why: The compound began as an adverb of direction, before it described the road itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词最初是方向副词，后来才用来形容路的本身。

senses.title: A difficult task that needs great effort
senses.definition: hard to achieve and demanding constant effort, as if climbing a slope
senses.definitionCN: 难以完成、需要持续投入力气的，仿佛是爬坡
senses.example: Persuading the council was an uphill struggle.
senses.exampleCN: 说服议会是一场艰苦的斗争。
senses.why: Anything that feels like pushing against a slope is called uphill, because the effort matches gravity.
senses.whyCN: 任何像逆着坡度用力的事都被说成 uphill，因为付出的力气正如在对抗重力。

senses.title: Moving or working higher on a hill
senses.titleCN: 在山上往高处走；往山坡上去
senses.definition: traveling or carrying something up a hillside
senses.definitionCN: 沿山斜坡向高处行走或搬运
senses.example: The farmers carried the grain uphill to the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 农民把粮食往山坡上挑，送到谷仓。
senses.why: This is the plain physical action from which the adjective and the figurative use both grow.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的实体动作，形容词义和比喻义都从这里长出来。

senses.title: The hard phase of a process
senses.definition: the part of an effort or recovery that requires the most work and shows the least progress
senses.definitionCN: 某项努力或恢复过程中最费力气、进展最慢的阶段
senses.example: The first month is always uphill before the work gets easier.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个月总是最吃力，之后工作才轻松些。
senses.why: A slope is hardest at the start, so uphill also names the tough early phase of any long effort.
senses.whyCN: 上坡起步最费力，所以 uphill 也指任何长期努力中最艰难的开头阶段。

intro.en: Uphill is a native English compound of the adverb up and the noun hill, recorded as a direction word long before its figurative use.
intro.cn: uphill 是本族英语复合词，由副词 up 与名词 hill 构成，先作为方向词出现，很久之后才有比喻用法。

items.en: Hill has an early English form hyll, meaning a raised piece of land, and up is a very old direction word.
items.cn: hill 在古英语早期作 hyll，指隆起的一块地；up 也是很古老的方向词。

items.en: Up and hill are joined in phrases of direction such as go up hill, describing movement toward higher ground.
items.cn: 中古英语用 up 加 hill 的方向短语，如 go up hill，表示朝高处走。

items.en: The written compound uphill is used for a rising road or an upward walk.
items.cn: 十六到十七世纪，连写的 uphill 用来指上坡的路或向上的行走。

items.en: Uphill extends from ground to effort, giving phrases such as an uphill struggle.
items.cn: 十九世纪，uphill 从地面延伸到努力，出现 an uphill struggle 这样的说法。

items.en: Today uphill is both a physical direction and a standard metaphor for hard work or difficulty.
items.cn: 如今 uphill 既是实体的方向，也是表示艰难与辛苦的固定比喻。

note.en: Uphill is a direction compound in the hill family and belongs to the field of effort and difficulty words.
note.cn: uphill 属于 hill 词族中的方向复合词，并归入表示努力与困难的义场。

entries.definition: a raised area of land
going toward a lower place
full of hills
needing a lot of effort
very tiring and demanding
rising sharply, hard to climb

normalIntro.en: See the parts: up gives the direction, hill gives the ground, and together they name the climb.
normalIntro.cn: 看清构件：up 给方向，hill 给地面，合起来就是往上爬的那段路。

normal.en: Up plus hill equals uphill, a road that goes upward.
normal.cn: up 加 hill 就是 uphill，一条朝上走的路。

normal.en: Downhill is its mirror twin: swap up for down and you get the easy descent.
normal.cn: downhill 是它的镜像：把 up 换成 down，就是轻松的下坡。

normal.en: Hill has a short adjective, hilly, and hill also appears in hillside and hilltop.
normal.cn: hill 的形容词是 hilly，它还出现在 hillside 与 hilltop 里。

normal.en: The nouns struggle, battle, and fight all pair with uphill: an uphill struggle, an uphill battle.
normal.cn: uphill 常与 struggle、battle、fight 搭配：an uphill struggle、an uphill battle。

normal.en: Compare steep: steep is about the angle, uphill is about the direction.
normal.cn: 对比 steep：steep 讲角度，uphill 讲方向。

abstract.en: Picture a cyclist standing on the pedals, pushing a loaded bike up a long lane.
abstract.cn: 想象一位骑行者站起蹬踏，推着载满货物的自行车爬上长坡道。

abstract.en: Imagine a signpost that points straight up and keeps rising out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象一块路标笔直朝上，一直伸到视线之外。

abstract.en: Think of a rock rolling against your hands as you try to push it higher.
abstract.cn: 想象你推石头上行，石头不断往回压你的手。

examples.en: The runners kept a steady pace on the uphill section.
examples.cn: 跑者在上坡路段保持了稳定的节奏。

examples.en: Learning a new language is an uphill task at first.
examples.cn: 学一门新语言起初是一桩费力的任务。

examples.en: We pushed the cart uphill under the midday sun.
examples.cn: 我们在正午的太阳下把车往坡上推。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普黑尔」——阿普背着黑行李箱爬坡，黑尔累得直喘；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hyll（山丘）加 up（向上）→ 中古英语方向短语 up hill → 英语 uphill（上坡的；向山上）。构词非常透明：up 表方向，hill 表地形，核心义由「向上」直接延伸到「费力」。

sensesIntro.en: Uphill begins as a direction word for ground that rises, then moves from the road to the effort of climbing it, so anything hard becomes uphill.
sensesIntro.cn: uphill 最初是表示地势升高的方向词，随后从路本身转到爬坡的力气，于是任何困难的事都能用 uphill 形容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body bent forward, pushing a load up a slope.
core.cn: 核心意象：身子前倾，把重物沿坡往上推。

branches.en: A rising road is the basic adjective sense.
branches.cn: 上升的道路是基本的形容词义项。

branches.en: Movement toward a higher point is the adverb sense.
branches.cn: 朝高处移动是副词义项。

branches.en: Hard tasks and hard phases borrow the effort of climbing.
branches.cn: 艰难的任务与艰难的阶段都借用了爬坡的力气。

branches.en: Carrying loads up a hillside is the plain physical action.
branches.cn: 把东西往山坡上运，是最朴素的实体动作。

branches.en: The road sense and the effort sense meet in the feeling of being pushed back.
branches.cn: 路的义项与费力的义项，在「被往后退」的感觉上汇合。

intro.en: Uphill is built from two free English words, the direction word up and the landscape noun hill.
intro.cn: uphill 由两个自由的英语词构成：方向词 up 与地形名词 hill。

latinIntro.en: Uphill is native English and Germanic in origin, without a Latin root, so no Latin family words are given.
latinIntro.cn: uphill 源自本族英语与日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.example: Up- gives the direction of the climb.
items.exampleCN: up- 给出向上爬的方向。

items.example: Hill names the ground the word refers to.
items.exampleCN: hill 指明所指的地形。

items.example: The compound keeps both parts visible.
items.exampleCN: 复合词的两个部分都还看得清。

items.example: Downhill reverses the first part.
items.exampleCN: downhill 把第一部分反了过来。

items.example: Hillside is built from hill and side.
items.exampleCN: hillside 由 hill 与 side 构成。

items.example: Hilltop marks the goal of the uphill walk.
items.exampleCN: hilltop 标出上坡路的终点。

items.example: The suffix -y makes an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成形容词。

items.example: The plural counts separate hills.
items.exampleCN: 复数用来数一座座小山。

definition_zh: 喧嚣；吵闹；哗然；骚动
definition_en: a loud confused noise made by many people at once, or an angry public protest or strong disagreement
core_image: 满屋的人同时拍桌大喊，声音像浪潮一样翻起来
scene: 比赛结果的判罚引来了全场观众的骂声和嘘声。The referee decision caused an uproar in the stadium.
sceneCN: 这里 uproar 取的是「喧嚣、吵闹」（第 1 个义项：多人同时发出的杂乱巨响）；句意：裁判的判罚在球场里引发了巨大的喧闹。

pos.zh: 喧嚣；吵闹；（公众的）哗然

derivatives.zh: 由 uproar 加 -ious 构成，义为「喧闹的；极为好笑的」
由 uproarious 加 -ly 构成，义为「哄堂大笑地」
词根动词，义为「吼叫；咆哮」
吼声；轰鸣，是 uproar 的核心名词

senses.title: A loud confused noise from many people
senses.definition: a very noisy and disordered sound made by a crowd at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 一大群人在同一时间发出的嘈杂而杂乱的声音
senses.example: The classroom rose to an uproar when the bell failed.
senses.exampleCN: 铃声没响，教室里顿时一片喧哗。
senses.why: Up means rising and roar is a beast cry, so an uproar is noise rising loudly from a crowd.
senses.whyCN: up 表示「升起」，roar 是野兽的吼声，所以 uproar 就是人群发出的、越来越高的声响。

senses.title: An angry public protest
senses.definition: a strong and noisy expression of public anger or disagreement about an event or decision
senses.definitionCN: 公众对某事件或决定表达出的强烈而喧嚷的不满与反对
senses.example: The price increase provoked a public uproar.
senses.exampleCN: 涨价引发了公众的强烈哗然。
senses.why: When outrage is loud enough, it becomes sound, so the noise word is borrowed for public anger.
senses.whyCN: 当愤慨足够响亮，就变成了声音，于是这个表示响声的词被借来说公众的愤怒。

senses.title: A state of noisy confusion or disorder
senses.definition: a troubled condition in which people are confused, angry, or out of control
senses.definitionCN: 人们困惑、愤怒或失去控制的不安状态
senses.example: The whole office was in an uproar after the leak.
senses.exampleCN: 消息泄露后整个办公室一片骚动。
senses.why: Besides the sound itself, uproar names the disturbed state that the noise reveals.
senses.whyCN: uproar 除了指声音本身，也指这片噪音所反映出的失序状态。

senses.title: Loud laughter
senses.definition: great bursts of noisy laughter from a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 一群人中爆发出的响亮的笑声
senses.example: The joke set the room in an uproar of laughter.
senses.exampleCN: 那个笑话让满屋人笑成一片。
senses.why: Laughter is also a roar, so an uproar can be a wave of happy noise rather than anger.
senses.whyCN: 笑声也是一种 roar，因此 uproar 可以是一阵欢乐的巨响，而不一定是愤怒。

senses.title: A loud disturbance of storm or wind
senses.definition: the roaring noise of a storm, strong wind, or boiling sea
senses.definitionCN: 暴风雨、狂风或翻腾的海水发出的轰鸣
senses.example: The night was filled with the uproar of the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 整夜都是风的呼啸声。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the roar root is the sound of an animal or of a storm, so nature can uproar too.
senses.whyCN: roar 词根最古老的意思就是野兽或风暴的响声，所以自然界也能「喧腾」。

intro.en: Uproar joins the adverb up with roar, but the older form uproar once carried the sense of a rising turbulence rather than simply noise.
intro.cn: uproar 由副词 up 与 roar 合成，较早的用法更多指翻起的动乱，而不只是纯粹的声音。

items.en: The roar family rests on an onomatopoeic Germanic base imitating a deep cry, with a reconstructed form often written as hrauzjan.
items.cn: roar 词族建立在日耳曼语中模仿低吼的拟声词基上，重构形式常写作 hrauzjan。

items.en: The noun roor or rour names the cry of animals and the crash of wind or water.
items.cn: 中古英语名词 roor 或 rour 指动物的吼声以及风水的轰鸣。

items.en: Uproar is recorded in the sixteenth century for a confused clamour raised by a crowd.
items.cn: 十六世纪，uproar 被记录用来指人群发出的杂乱喊闹。

items.en: The word spreads from physical noise to public anger expressed loudly.
items.cn: 这个词从实体噪音延伸到大声表达的公众愤怒。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the noise sense and the angry protest sense, and adds lively laughter.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留声响义与愤怒抗议义，并延伸出热烈的笑声。

note.en: Uproar shares the roar family and sits close to clamour and din in the noise field, and near outrage in the protest field.
note.cn: uproar 与 roar 同根，在噪音义场中与 clamour、din 相邻，在抗议义场中与 outrage 相近。

entries.definition: to make a long deep loud sound
very noisy or very funny
in a very noisy or comic way
a loud confused noise from many voices
a loud unpleasant continuous noise
strong public anger and shock

normalIntro.en: Uproar is transparent: up for rising, roar for the loud cry, so the noise literally rises out of the crowd.
normalIntro.cn: uproar 一目了然：up 表上升，roar 表吼叫，噪音就从人群里升起来。

normal.en: A lion roars, and a crowd roars too; uproar is the crowd version.
normal.cn: 狮子会 roar（咆哮），人群也会 roar；uproar 就是人群版。

normal.en: Up gives the direction, so the sound is rising and spreading upward.
normal.cn: up 给出方向，声音是往上涌、往外扩的。

normal.en: The adjective is uproarious, used for something very funny as well as very noisy.
normal.cn: 形容词是 uproarious，既形容吵闹，也形容非常搞笑。

normal.en: Learn it with cause an uproar and in an uproar: the first is the trigger, the second is the state.
normal.cn: 连着 cause an uproar 与 in an uproar 记：前者是起因，后者是状态。

normal.en: Compare din: din is steady unpleasant noise, uproar is people reacting together.
normal.cn: 对比 din：din 是持续难听的噪音，uproar 是一群人一起反应出的声响。

abstract.en: Picture a stadium where thousands of people stand and shout at the same second.
abstract.cn: 想象一整座球场，上千人在同一秒站起来大喊。

abstract.en: Imagine a wave of sound rolling over the seats and shaking the fences.
abstract.cn: 想象一道声浪滚过看台，把围栏都震得发颤。

abstract.en: Think of a kettle lid rattling because everything inside is boiling and rising.
abstract.cn: 想象水壶盖被顶得乱跳，因为壶里全在翻滚上涌。

examples.en: The plan to close the library caused an uproar among residents.
examples.cn: 关闭图书馆的计划在居民中引起一片哗然。

examples.en: His comic timing left the audience in an uproar of laughter.
examples.cn: 他的喜剧节奏让观众笑成一片。

examples.en: There was an uproar in the hall when the winner was named.
examples.cn: 宣布获胜者时，大厅里一片喧腾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普罗」——阿普在广场上放声大嚷，普罗被吵得捂着耳朵跑开；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 roor / rour（吼声、轰鸣，拟声词）加 up（向上）→ 英语 uproar（升起的喧闹）。roar 与大型兽类的吼叫有关，up 表示声音向上升腾，核心义是「嘈杂声冒起来」。

sensesIntro.en: Uproar starts as the loud noise of many voices, then becomes public anger, disorder, laughter, and finally the roar of a storm.
sensesIntro.cn: uproar 从众人齐声的响亮噪音出发，继而指公众愤怒、失序、笑声，最后还能指风暴的呼啸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sound rising like a wave out of a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：声音像浪一样从人群里涌起。

branches.en: The plain loud crowd noise is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 人群杂乱的巨响是基本义项。

branches.en: Public anger made audible is the protest sense.
branches.cn: 把公众愤怒说出口，就是抗议义项。

branches.en: The disturbed state behind the noise is the disorder sense.
branches.cn: 噪音背后的失序状态，就是骚动义项。

branches.en: Laughter and storm wind both use the same rising roar image.
branches.cn: 笑声与风暴呼啸都用同一个「涌起的轰鸣」意象。

branches.en: Noise and protest often arrive together, since anger needs a voice.
branches.cn: 声响与抗议常常同时出现，因为愤怒需要出声。

intro.en: Uproar is a two-word build with the direction word up and the verb and noun roar at its heart.
intro.cn: uproar 由两个词合成：方向词 up，加上核心的动词兼名词 roar。

latinIntro.en: Uproar is Germanic and onomatopoeic in origin and has no Latin root, so no Latin family words are listed.
latinIntro.cn: uproar 来自日耳曼语并带拟声性质，没有拉丁词根，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.example: Up- pushes the sound upward.
items.exampleCN: up- 把声音往上推。

items.meaning: to make a deep loud cry
items.example: Roar supplies the noise at the centre.
items.exampleCN: roar 提供词义中心的响声。

items.example: The compound is the everyday word for clamour.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是表示喧嚷的日常用语。

items.example: The plural counts separate scenes of noise.
items.exampleCN: 复数用来数一场场喧闹。

items.example: The suffix -ious forms upside-down uproarious.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ious 构成形容词 uproarious。

items.example: Uproarious describes a happy uproar.
items.exampleCN: uproarious 形容欢乐的喧闹。

items.example: The suffix -ly makes an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词。

items.example: Uproariously often pairs with funny.
items.exampleCN: uproariously 常与 funny 搭配。

definition_zh: 高档的；高阶的；使升级；使高档化；使（产品、企业、系统）扩大规模或提升层级
definition_en: high in quality or aimed at wealthy customers, or to raise the quality, size or level of something
core_image: 一把梯子的每一格都往上抬，原本朴素的小店换上了金子招牌
scene: 老街上一家朴素的小餐馆，悄悄换掉了塑料桌布。The family decided to upscale the restaurant with better food and higher prices.
sceneCN: 这里 upscale 是「使高档化」（第 6 个义项：把小本经营的场所改造成面向高消费顾客的地方）；句意是这家人决定用更好的菜色与更高的价格来提升餐馆档次。画面里是旧塑料桌布、新餐椅与菜单。

pos.zh: 高档的；高消费的；高阶的；上移的
提升……的档次；使（产品、企业）升级；扩大规模

collocations.zh: 把一家企业往高端升级

derivatives.zh: 由 upscale 加动名词后缀构成，义为「升级；提档；规模扩大」
由 upscale 加表施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「提档的投资者或经营者」
与 upscale 词素对调而成的复合名词，义为「规模化扩大」

senses.title: High in quality and aimed at the rich
senses.definition: expensive and of high quality, usually aimed at wealthy customers
senses.definitionCN: 价格昂贵、品质高，通常面向有钱的顾客
senses.example: They booked a room in an upscale hotel near the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在湖边一家高档酒店订了房间。
senses.why: Up puts the word at the top of a scale, so upscale means high up on the scale of quality and price.
senses.whyCN: up 把词义推到一把尺子的顶端，所以 upscale 指在品质与价格的标尺上位置很高。

senses.title: To raise the quality or level of something
senses.definition: to improve the quality, design or level of something so that it suits a higher market
senses.definitionCN: 改进某物的品质、设计或水平，使它适合更高端的市场
senses.example: The brand upscaled its packaging to attract younger buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌升级了包装，以吸引更年轻的买家。
senses.why: The verb reads up and scale as a small phrase, so acting on a thing means moving it up the scale.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时 up 与 scale 相当于一个小短语，对某物动手就是把它往上移到尺子更高的位置。

senses.title: Of a district or a place that has become expensive
senses.definition: describing an area or a building where prices and incomes have risen and cheaper shops have gone
senses.definitionCN: 描述价格与收入上升、便宜店铺已被挤走的街区或建筑
senses.example: The old market street is now an upscale area.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧市场街如今成了高消费地段。
senses.why: The place itself climbs the price scale, so the adjective describes a district that has moved up, not one that was always rich.
senses.whyCN: 地方本身沿价格标尺往上爬，所以这个形容词描述的是被抬上去的街区，而不是一向富裕的街区。

senses.title: To move jobs or staff to a higher grade
senses.definition: to move a job, a worker or a role to a higher grade or level within an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 把职位、员工或角色在企业或机构中移到更高等级
senses.example: The firm upscaled the post from assistant to manager.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把这个职位从助理升为经理。
senses.why: A ladder of grades is itself a scale, and upscale means shifting a post one step higher on it.
senses.whyCN: 职级阶梯本身就是一把 scale（刻度尺），upscale 就是把职位沿着它往上挪一格。

senses.title: To enlarge an image electronically
senses.definition: to enlarge a digital image or video while keeping it sharp, often with software that guesses missing detail
senses.definitionCN: 放大数字图像或视频并尽量保持清晰，常靠软件补出缺失的细节
senses.example: The app upscaled the old photograph to a large size without blurring it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用把那张老照片放大到大尺寸，也没有变糊。
senses.why: Scale in computing means the size an image is drawn at, so upscale is literally to turn the scale up.
senses.whyCN: 电脑里的 scale 指图像被画出来时的尺寸，所以 upscale 字面上就是把尺寸调大。

senses.title: To turn a modest business into a high-end one
senses.titleCN: 使高档化；把小本生意做高级
senses.definition: to improve and reprice a small shop, caf or hotel so that it serves wealthier customers
senses.definitionCN: 改进小商店、咖啡馆或旅馆并调高价格，让它们服务更有钱的顾客
senses.example: New owners upscale the caf but keep the old wooden counter.
senses.exampleCN: 新老板把咖啡馆做了提档，却保留了那张旧木柜台。
senses.why: The object is a whole business, and the change is a climb in price, service and custom rather than a single repair.
senses.whyCN: 对象是一整门生意，变动的是价格、服务与客源的整体抬升，而不是某一处修补。

intro.en: Upscale is a modern English compound of the adverb up and the noun scale, built on the Latin root scala, a ladder or flight of steps.
intro.cn: upscale 是英语里由副词 up 与名词 scale 拼成的现代复合词，scale 又出自拉丁语 scala（梯子、台阶）。

items.en: Scala meant ladder or flight of steps, and its plural scalae were the rungs one climbs.
items.cn: scala 意为梯子、台阶，其复数 scalae 就是一格一格可攀的台阶。

items.en: Medieval Latin used scalae for a graded series, and that graded idea later spread into measurement.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用 scalae 指分级的序列，这种「分级」的观念后来扩展到测量之中。

items.en: English scale first meant a ladder or steps, then a measuring rule, then the range of a system such as its size or level; the measurement senses are recorded from the late sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语 scale 先指梯子、台阶，再指测量用的刻度尺，进而指一个体系的规模或等级范围；测量相关的义项自十六世纪后期有记录。

items.en: In trade and computing, scale came to mean the size of an operation or the size of an image, which gave the phrasal verbs scale up and scale down.
items.cn: 在商业与计算机领域，scale 进而指经营规模或图像尺寸，由此产生短语动词 scale up 与 scale down。

items.en: The single word upscale appeared in the twentieth century, first as an adjective for expensive goods and then as a verb; exact first dates are not settled.
items.cn: 合写而成的 upscale 一词出现于二十世纪，先指昂贵货物的形容词，随后作动词使用；确切首见年代尚无定论。

items.en: Housing reports and image software popularised upscale area and upscaled picture, extending the word to places and pixels.
items.cn: 房产报道与图像软件让 upscale area 与 upscaled picture 流行开来，把这个词扩展到街区与像素上。

note.en: Upscale sits next to words built on the same scale, such as escala and escalation, and beside ordinary words for raising quality.
note.cn: upscale 与同一把 scale（刻度尺）的 escalator、escalation 相邻，也与一般的「提高品质」词相邻。

entries.definition: to become or make more serious or intense
a rise in intensity or seriousness
a moving staircase
great comfort or expensive things that are not necessary
of higher quality and higher price than usual
designed for rich or demanding customers

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real scale root and the common phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 scale 词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Up and scale read together as moving up a scale, which is exactly the compound meaning.
normal.cn: 把 up 与 scale 连起来读，就是沿着刻度尺往上走，这正是这个复合词的意思。

normal.en: Scale comes from Latin scala, a ladder, so an upscale hotel sits higher on the ladder of price.
normal.cn: scale 出自拉丁语 scala（梯子），所以一家 upscale 酒店在价格的梯子上站得更高。

normal.en: Escalate, escalation and escalator share the same step image, and they all climb.
normal.cn: escalate、escalation、escalator 共享同一个台阶意象，它们都在往上爬。

normal.en: Upscale stores the adjective, while to upscale is the verb, so a shop can upscale its menu.
normal.cn: upscale 可作形容词，也可作动词，所以一家店可以 upscale 自己的菜单。

normal.en: Its opposite partner is downscale, and the phrasal pair is scale up and scale down.
normal.cn: 与它相对的搭档是 downscale，短语形式则是 scale up 与 scale down。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose rungs are price tags: upscale is the top rung.
abstract.cn: 想象一把梯子，每一格都是价签：upscale 就是最上面那一格。

abstract.en: Picture hands pushing a small shop one rung higher on that ladder, swapping plastic for wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手把一家小店沿那把梯子往上推一格，塑料换成了木头。

abstract.en: Picture a whole street climbing together, so the old corner shop turns into a bright bistro.
abstract.cn: 想象整条街一起往上爬，街角的老铺子变成了明亮的餐馆。

examples.en: The new metro station has brought upscale shops to the old neighbourhood.
examples.cn: 新地铁站给这个老街区带来了高档商店。

examples.en: Investors plan to upscale the small farm into a modern food company.
examples.cn: 投资者打算把那家小农场升级为现代食品公司。

examples.en: The software upscaled the blurred image without adding artificial detail.
examples.cn: 这款软件把模糊的图像放大了，却没有添加虚假的细节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普斯盖尔」——往上（up）爬梯子（scale），一格一格抬起来：越高档，越往上升；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 up（向上）+ scale（刻度、等级；源出拉丁语 scala「梯子、台阶」），合写为 upscale，核心是「沿着刻度往上抬一档」。与 escalate、escalator 同出一把梯子。

sensesIntro.en: One image runs through all six senses: the scale rises. It starts with goods priced high, then moves to the act of raising them, a district that has risen, a post moved up a grade, an image enlarged on a screen, and a whole business turned high-end.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项共用同一个意象：标尺往上抬。它先是「价格高」的物品，再是「把某物抬上去」的动作，接着是已抬高的街区、被升格的职位、在屏幕上放大的图像，以及被整体做成高端的生意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ladder of price tags, with a small plain shop being pushed one rung higher.
core.cn: 核心意象：一连串价签组成的梯子，一家朴素小店正被往上推一格。

branches.en: Goods and services at the top of the price scale give the plain adjective.
branches.cn: 处于价格标尺顶端的商品与服务，构成这个形容词的基本义。

branches.en: The action sense treats the compound as a verb and pushes a thing higher on that scale.
branches.cn: 动作义把这个复合词当动词用，把某物沿标尺往上推。

branches.en: A district climbs the scale as a whole, so the adjective can describe a place that has risen.
branches.cn: 一个街区整体沿标尺上移，于是这个形容词也能描述被抬高的地方。

branches.en: A ladder of job grades is a scale too, so a post can be moved one step up.
branches.cn: 职级阶梯同样是一把 scale，因此职位可以被往上挪一格。

branches.en: The newest branches widen the scale to pixels and to whole businesses.
branches.cn: 最新的分支把标尺延伸到像素，也延伸到整门生意。

intro.en: Upscale is formed by compounding, not by a suffix: the adverb up is set against the noun scale, the same scale found in escalate and scaler.
intro.cn: upscale 靠复合而非后缀构成：副词 up 与名词 scale 并置，与 escalate、scaler 中的 scale 同源。

latinIntro.en: Latin scala, a ladder, is recorded, and so is its plural scalae; the deeper origin of scala itself is not settled.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scala「梯子」及其复数 scalae 均有记录；scala 更早的来源尚无定论。

items.meaning: towards a higher position or level
items.example: The prefix pushes the whole word up a level.
items.exampleCN: 这个前项把整个词抬高一个层级。

items.meaning: a range of levels, sizes or prices
items.meaningCN: 等级、规模或价格的刻度范围
items.example: The noun supplies the ladder image.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供梯子的意象。

items.example: Scala is the recorded Latin source of scale.
items.exampleCN: scala 是有记录的拉丁语来源。

items.example: The plural stresses the separate rungs.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式强调一格一格的台阶。

items.example: The ending forms escalate in the same family.
items.exampleCN: 同一词族里这个词尾构成 escalate。

items.example: Escalate also climbs from the ladder image.
items.exampleCN: escalate 也从梯子意象往上爬。

items.example: The noun keeps the upward movement.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词保留了向上的移动。

items.example: The plural is used in price scales.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式用在价格刻度这类说法里。

items.example: The participle describes a picture or a shop already raised.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词描述已经完成的提档或放大。

definition_zh: 利用；使用；利用率；动用；发挥效用
definition_en: the act of using something, especially a resource, in an effective way, or the rate at which something is used
core_image: 一只水桶把水池里的水舀起来，倒进田里的沟渠，让每滴水都派上用场
scene: 实验田旁边放着种子、化肥和水管，负责人先清点了家底。Careful utilisation of water helped the farm survive the dry summer.
sceneCN: 这里 utilisation 是「利用」（第 2 个义项：把资源充分有效地用起来）；句意是精打细算地用水让农场熬过了干旱的夏天。画面里有种子袋、化肥袋与水管。

pos.zh: 利用；使用；利用率；动用；发挥效用

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -ation 得到的动词，义为「利用；使用」
由 utilise 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可利用的；可使用的」
由本词加 rate 构成的复合名词，义为「利用率」

senses.title: The act of using something
senses.definition: the act of using a thing, tool or service for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为了某个目的而使用某物、某工具或某项服务的行为
senses.example: The utilisation of mobile phones in class is not allowed.
senses.exampleCN: 课堂上不允许使用手机。
senses.why: The Latin verb uti means to use, so the whole family starts from the plain act of using.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 uti 意为使用，整个词族都从这个最朴素的动作出发。

senses.title: The effective use of a resource
senses.definition: the practical use of a natural or economic resource so that it serves a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 对自然或经济资源加以实际使用，使其产生作用
senses.example: Better utilisation of farmland could raise the region incomes.
senses.exampleCN: 更好地利用耕地可以提高这一地区的收入。
senses.why: Utile in Latin means useful, so the noun pushes the plain act towards making something yield value.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 utile 意为有用的，所以这个名词把一般的使用推向「让某物产生价值」。

senses.title: The rate at which capacity is used
senses.definition: the percentage of a machine, building or workforce that is actually in use
senses.definitionCN: 机器、建筑或劳动力实际被使用的比例
senses.example: The factory raised capacity utilisation above ninety per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把产能利用率提高到了九成以上。
senses.why: Once the act of using is counted, the noun naturally becomes a figure: how much of the whole is being put to work.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把「使用」这件事加以计量，名词自然变成数字：整体中有多大比例被投入使用。

senses.title: The putting to work of a skill or idea
senses.definition: the application of a skill, a method or an idea in practice
senses.definitionCN: 把技能、方法或创意实际运用到实践中
senses.example: Her clever utilisation of simple materials won the design prize.
senses.exampleCN: 她巧妙运用简单材料，赢得了设计奖。
senses.why: The object of use need not be a physical resource: skills and ideas are things that can be put to work.
senses.whyCN: 被使用的对象不必是物质资源：技能与创意同样是可以「派上用场」的对象。

senses.title: The share of a pool of funds or energy that is spent
senses.definition: the proportion of an available sum of money or supply of energy that is actually spent or consumed
senses.definitionCN: 可用的资金总额或能源总量中，实际花掉或消耗掉的那一部分
senses.example: The report tracks the utilisation of the transport budget each quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告每季度追踪交通预算的动用情况。
senses.why: Money and power behave like a stored supply, and utilisation records how much of that supply has been drawn.
senses.whyCN: 资金和电力都像存量供给，utilisation 记录的就是这份供给被取走了多少。

intro.en: Utilisation is a noun built on the Latin adjective utilis, useful, which comes from uti, to use, itself with the adjective participle form usus. The noun ending -ation came through French.
intro.cn: utilisation 是建立在拉丁语形容词 utilis（有用的）之上的名词，utilis 又出自 uti（使用），并带有分词形式 usus；名词词尾 -ation 经法语传来。

items.en: The verb uti is generally linked, as a reconstructed form, to a root meaning to use or enjoy; the deeper origin of that root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为动词 uti 可追溯到一个意为「使用、享用」的原始印欧语词根，属于重构形式；该词根更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Uti meant to use or make use of a thing, and its participle usus gave the noun usus, a use.
items.cn: uti 意为使用某物或加以利用，其分词形式 usus 又给出名词 usus（使用）。

items.en: The adjective utilis took the verb stem and the ending -ilis, meaning that may be used, so useful.
items.cn: 形容词 utilis 在动词词干后接词尾 -ilis，意为「可被使用的」，即有用的。

items.en: The noun utilitas meant usefulness or utility; it is the pattern that later English nouns copied.
items.cn: 名词 utilitas 意为有用性、效用，后来英语的名词正是照着这个模式构成的。

items.en: French formed nouns in -ation from verbs in -iser, and the pattern brought utilise and utilisation to English.
items.cn: 法语用 -iser 动词加 -ation 构成名词，这个模式把 utilise 与 utilisation 带进英语。

items.en: Industrial and statistical writing made utilisation a routine noun for how fully resources are used, and its exact first date is not settled.
items.cn: 工业与统计写作使 utilisation 成为说明资源使用程度的常用名词，其确切首见年代尚无定论。

note.en: Utilisation keeps the Latin useful root, so it stands beside utile, utilis and the -ize family, and beside ordinary words for use and efficiency.
note.cn: utilisation 保留了拉丁语「有用」词根，因此与 utile、utilis 及 -ize 词族相邻，也与一般的「使用」「效率」词相邻。

entries.definition: to use something, especially effectively
usefulness, or a public service such as gas
useful rather than beautiful
to employ something for a purpose
the using up of goods or energy
working well with little waste

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root uti and the set phrases the noun actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 uti，以及这个名词实际出现的固定说法。

normal.en: Uti is to use, and utilis means useful; utilisation is the noun that names using a thing usefully.
normal.cn: uti 是使用，utilis 是有用的；utilisation 就是「把有用之物用起来」的名词。

normal.en: The -ation ending turns the verb utilise into the act, so utilise and utilisation always travel together.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ation 把动词 utilise 变成动作之名，所以 utilise 与 utilisation 总是成对出现。

normal.en: Utility, utilize and utilisation share one root, and they all point at usefulness.
normal.cn: utility、utilize 与 utilisation 共享一个词根，都指向有用性。

normal.en: Capacity utilisation is a percentage, the share of a machine that is working.
normal.cn: capacity utilisation 是一个百分比，即机器真正在工作的比例。

normal.en: British writing keeps the -s- spelling utilisation, and American writing uses -z- instead.
normal.cn: 英式写法保留 -s- 的 utilisation，美式则改用 -z-。

abstract.en: Picture a bucket lifting water from a pool and pouring it into a field channel.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水桶把池水舀起，倒进田间的沟渠。

abstract.en: Picture a dial that shows how much of a tank has been drawn off, with the needle near full.
abstract.cn: 想象一只计量表，显示水箱里的水被取走了多少，指针几乎到达顶格。

abstract.en: Picture a row of workers and machines with only one or two gaps, the rest all busy.
abstract.cn: 想象一排工人和机器，其中只空着一两台，其余都在忙碌。

examples.en: The study compares water utilisation in cities and in rural areas.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较了城市与农村的用水情况。

examples.en: Low utilisation of the new library worried the local council.
examples.cn: 新图书馆使用率偏低，让当地议会很担心。

examples.en: Firms that improve energy utilisation often cut their costs sharply.
examples.cn: 提高能源利用率的公司往往能大幅削减成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优提来神」——把有用的东西「优质地提」起来「利用」，一滴都不浪费；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 uti（使用）→ utilis（有用的）→ 法语 -iser 与 -ation 构词 → 英语 utilise（利用）→ utilisation（利用；利用率）。核心义「把有用之物用起来」，是 use 的正式同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Utilisation grows out of one plain act of using. First it is any act of use, then the use of resources, then the measured rate of that use, then the putting to work of skills, and finally the share of a budget or supply that has been drawn on.
sensesIntro.cn: utilisation 从「使用」这一个朴素动作生长出来：先是任何一次使用，然后是资源的利用，接着是把这种使用量化的利用率，再是技能与创意的运用，最后是资金或能源被动用的比例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bucket lifts water from a pool and pours it into a field channel until every drop is put to work.
core.cn: 核心意象：水桶从池子里舀水，倒进田间沟渠，让每一滴水都派上用场。

branches.en: Any act of using something is the plainest sense of the noun.
branches.cn: 任何一次「使用」都是这个名词最朴素的意义。

branches.en: Focused on resources, the act becomes the practical turning of land, water or energy to use.
branches.cn: 聚焦到资源上，这个动作就变成把土地、水或能源实际用起来。

branches.en: Counted against a total, the act becomes a rate such as capacity utilisation.
branches.cn: 与总量相比，这个动作就变成产能利用率这类比率。

branches.en: When skills or ideas are the thing used, the noun names their practical application.
branches.cn: 当被使用的是技能或创意时，这个名词指的是它们的实际运用。

branches.en: Budget and energy are drawn like water from a pool, so the noun records the share drawn.
branches.cn: 预算与能源像池水一样被取用，于是这个名词记录被取走的份额。

intro.en: Utilisation stacks a Latin verb stem, a Latin adjective ending and the French noun ending -ation; English also has the verb utilise and the adjective utilisable.
intro.cn: utilisation 叠合了拉丁动词词干、拉丁形容词词尾与法语名词词尾 -ation；英语还有动词 utilise 与形容词 utilisable。

latinIntro.en: Latin uti, usus, utilis and utilitas are all recorded; only the deeper Indo-European root is a reconstructed form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 uti、usus、utilis 与 utilitas 均有文献记录，只有更早的原始印欧语词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The verb uti is the oldest member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 动词 uti 是这个词族里最古老的成员。

items.example: The participle form usus links the family to English use.
items.exampleCN: 分词形式 usus 把这一词族与英语 use 连起来。

items.example: Utilis is the recorded source of the English family.
items.exampleCN: utilis 是英语这一词族有记录的来源。

items.example: The noun utilitas is the model behind utility.
items.exampleCN: 名词 utilitas 是 utility 的构词范本。

items.example: The ending -ilis forms utilis from uti.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ilis 由 uti 构成 utilis。

items.example: Utilise is the verb that utilisation names.
items.exampleCN: utilise 就是 utilisation 所指的那个动作。

items.example: The suffix -ise forms utilise in British spelling.
items.exampleCN: 英式拼写里词尾 -ise 构成 utilise。

items.structure: noun ending through French and Latin
items.example: The ending -ation forms utilisation from utilise.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 由 utilise 构成 utilisation。

items.example: The suffix -able forms utilisable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 utilisable。

definition_zh: 利用；使用；运用；动用；发挥……的效用
definition_en: to put something to practical use, especially a resource, a method or an opportunity
core_image: 木匠把角落里的旧木板锯开，钉成一张能用的桌子
scene: 工地的旧木材原本堆在墙角，眼看要被扔掉。The builders decided to utilise the leftover timber for new benches.
sceneCN: 这里 utilise 是「利用」（第 2 个义项：把现成的资源派上实际用场）；句意是施工队决定把剩下的木料用来做新长凳。画面里是堆在墙角的木板、锯子和一张刚钉好的凳子。

pos.zh: 利用；使用；运用；动用；发挥……的效用

derivatives.zh: 由 utilise 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「利用；利用率」
由 utilise 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可利用的；可使用的」
由 utilise 加表施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「使用者；利用者」

senses.title: To use something
senses.definition: to use a tool, a system or a piece of equipment, often in a formal or technical report
senses.definitionCN: 使用某工具、系统或设备，常用于正式或技术性叙述
senses.example: The new lab utilises the latest imaging equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 新实验室使用最新的成像设备。
senses.why: The Latin verb uti means to use, so utilise begins with the plain act of making use of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 uti 意为使用，所以 utilise 一开始就是指「把某物用起来」这个朴素动作。

senses.title: To make practical use of a resource
senses.definition: to turn land, water, money or material to practical account instead of letting it go to waste
senses.definitionCN: 把土地、水、资金或材料派上实际用场，而不是任其浪费
senses.example: Farmers utilise rainwater to irrigate the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 农民利用雨水灌溉田地。
senses.why: It comes from utilis, useful, so the act is framed as turning an idle thing into something that yields value.
senses.whyCN: 它出自 utilis（有用的），因此这个动作被框定为把闲置之物变为能产出价值的东西。

senses.title: To apply a method or a skill
senses.definition: to apply a method, a technique or a skill in order to achieve a result
senses.definitionCN: 为实现某个结果而运用某种方法、技术或技能
senses.example: Students who utilise good note-taking methods revise faster.
senses.exampleCN: 善于运用良好记笔记方法的学生复习得更快。
senses.why: Methods and skills are tools in the abstract sense, so using them is the same act applied to something invisible.
senses.whyCN: 方法与技能是抽象意义上的工具，运用它们就是把同一个动作施加在看不见的东西上。

senses.title: To take advantage of an opportunity
senses.definition: to make good use of a chance, a situation or an advantage while it is available
senses.definitionCN: 在机会、形势或优势还在手边时充分利用它
senses.example: She utilised the quiet morning hours to finish the report.
senses.exampleCN: 她利用清晨安静的时间完成了报告。
senses.why: A chance is also a resource that can be spent or wasted, so utilise takes it as its object.
senses.whyCN: 机会同样是一种可以花掉也可能浪费的资源，所以 utilise 可以以它为对象。

senses.title: To manage or spend money and materials
senses.definition: to put a sum of money or a stock of material into use, often in a budget or a project
senses.definitionCN: 把一笔钱或一批材料投入使用，常见于预算或项目叙述
senses.example: The council utilised part of its budget to repair the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 议会动用了部分预算来修缮那座桥。
senses.why: Money and material are stored supplies, and using them is releasing that store into work; the word suits official accounts.
senses.whyCN: 资金与材料是储备着的供给，使用它们就是把这份储备投入运作；这个词适合官方账目。

intro.en: Utilise is the English verb made from the French and Italian verb-forming pattern on Latin utilis, useful, from uti, to use; American spelling writes it utilize.
intro.cn: utilise 是英语依照法语与意大利语加动词词尾的模式、从拉丁语 utilis（有用的）造出的动词，utilis 又出自 uti（使用）；美式拼写写作 utilize。

items.en: The verb uti is generally traced, as a reconstructed form, to a root meaning to use or enjoy; the deeper origin of that root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为动词 uti 可追溯到意为「使用、享用」的原始印欧语词根，属于重构形式；该词根更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Uti meant to use or enjoy, and it is the oldest recorded member of the family.
items.cn: uti 意为使用或享用，是这一词族里有记录的最古老的成员。

items.en: The adjective utilis means useful, and the noun utilitas means usefulness; the second group gives English utility and utilitarian.
items.cn: 形容词 utilis 意为有用的，名词 utilitas 意为有用性；这一组词给英语带来 utility 与 utilitarian。

items.en: Italian formed a verb on utilise-like material with the productive ending -are, meaning to turn something to use.
items.cn: 意大利语用一个能产的词尾 -are 造出意为「把某物转为使用」的动词。

items.en: French utiliser carried the verb into administrative and technical writing, and English borrowed the pattern from it.
items.cn: 法语 utiliser 把这个动词带进行政与技术写作，英语又从它借用了这一模式。

items.en: English formed utilise in the nineteenth century, and it soon became the formal partner of use; exact first dates are not settled.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪造出 utilise，它很快成为 use 的正式搭档；确切首见年代尚无定论。

note.en: Utilise is the verb at the centre of the useful family, with utilisation, utility and utiliseable around it, and with use and employ as its plainer neighbours.
note.cn: utilise 是「有用」这一词族的中心动词，周围有 utilisation、utility 等词，更朴素的近邻则是 use 与 employ。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same verb
the act of using something
designed to be useful rather than beautiful
to use a tool, method or person
to use something fully, often unfairly
to put a method or a skill into practice

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root uti and the collocations the verb actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 uti，以及这个动词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Uti is to use, and utilis is useful, so utilise means to put a useful thing to work.
normal.cn: uti 是使用，utilis 是有用的，所以 utilise 意为把有用之物投入运作。

normal.en: Utilise, utilisation and utility share one root, so hearing utilisation is hearing the verb.
normal.cn: utilise、utilisation 与 utility 共享一个词根，听到 utilisation 就等于听到这个动词。

normal.en: Utilise is the formal cousin of use; a report may utilise a method, a friend just uses it.
normal.cn: utilise 是 use 的正式表亲：报告会 utilise 某种方法，朋友只是直接 use 它。

normal.en: British writing keeps the -ise ending and American writing keeps -ize, so utilise and utilize are one verb.
normal.cn: 英式写作保留 -ise 词尾，美式则用 -ize，所以 utilise 与 utilize 是同一个动词。

normal.en: To utilise a resource fully is the aim each time the noun utilisation appears in a report.
normal.cn: 报告里每次出现 utilisation，目标都是 fully utilise（充分利用）某项资源。

abstract.en: Picture a carpenter cutting an old board into a sturdy table leg.
abstract.cn: 想象木匠把一块旧木板锯成结实的桌腿。

abstract.en: Picture a rain barrel on a roof, catching water that would otherwise run down the street.
abstract.cn: 想象屋顶上的接雨桶，接住原本会流到街上的雨水。

abstract.en: Picture a student opening a drawer of old notes and turning them into a neat revision plan.
abstract.cn: 想象学生拉开装满旧笔记的抽屉，把它们整理成一份清晰的复习计划。

examples.en: Many villages utilise solar panels to run their water pumps.
examples.cn: 许多村庄使用太阳能板来驱动水泵。

examples.en: The teacher encourages pupils to utilise library resources for the project.
examples.cn: 老师鼓励学生利用图书馆资源来完成这个课题。

examples.en: Good teams utilise every minute of the planning meeting.
examples.cn: 优秀的团队会把规划会议的每一分钟都用起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「有提来用」——把有用的东西「提」出来「用」上，不浪费；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 uti（使用）→ utilis（有用的）→ 意大利语 utilizzare、法语 utiliser 的动词模式 → 英语 utilise（利用）/ utilize。核心义「把有用之物派上用场」，比 use 更正式，近亲有 utilisation、utility、utilitarian。

sensesIntro.en: Utilise runs from the plain act of using an object, through the practical use of resources, methods and chances, to the official spending of money and material.
sensesIntro.cn: utilise 从「使用一件物品」这个朴素动作出发，经过对资源、方法与机会的实际利用，一路延伸到官方账目里对资金与材料的动用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carpenter takes an old board from the corner and turns it into a working table.
core.cn: 核心意象：木匠从墙角取下一块旧木板，把它做成一张能用的桌子。

branches.en: The plain act of using a tool or a system is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 使用工具或系统这个朴素动作是最日常的义项。

branches.en: Directed at land, water or material, the act becomes the practical use of a resource.
branches.cn: 当对象是土地、水或材料时，这个动作就变成对资源的实际利用。

branches.en: A method or a skill is a tool in the abstract, so the same verb applies to them.
branches.cn: 方法与技能是抽象意义上的工具，同一个动词也能用在它们身上。

branches.en: An opportunity can be spent or wasted like a supply, so it can be utilised as well.
branches.cn: 机会可以像供给一样被用掉或浪费，因此也可以 utilise。

branches.en: In official accounts, budgets and stocks of material are drawn on, so the verb turns into formal spending language.
branches.cn: 在官方账目中，预算与材料存量被取用，于是这个动词变成正式的支出用语。

intro.en: Utilise is a Latin verb stem uti with an adjective ending and a Romance verb ending; English adds -ation, -able and -er to build the family.
intro.cn: utilise 由拉丁动词词干 uti 加上形容词词尾与罗曼语动词词尾构成；英语再加 -ation、-able 与 -er 扩展出这个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin uti, usus, utilis and utilitas are recorded forms; only the Indo-European root behind uti is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 uti、usus、utilis 与 utilitas 都是有记录的形式，只有 uti 背后的原始印欧语词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The Latin verb uti is the root of the whole group.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁动词 uti 是这一组词的总词根。

items.example: Utilis means useful and gives the English stem.
items.exampleCN: utilis 意为有用的，提供英语词干。

items.example: The noun utilitas is the model behind utility.
items.exampleCN: 名词 utilitas 是 utility 的构词范本。

items.example: The ending -ilis forms utilis from uti.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ilis 由 uti 构成 utilis。

items.example: The French ending -iser forms utiliser.
items.exampleCN: 法语词尾 -iser 构成 utiliser。

items.example: The ending -ise forms utilise in British English.
items.exampleCN: 英式英语里词尾 -ise 构成 utilise。

items.example: The ending -ize forms utilize in American English.
items.exampleCN: 美式英语里词尾 -ize 构成 utilize。

items.structure: noun ending through French and Latin
items.example: The ending -ation forms utilisation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 utilisation。

items.example: The suffix -able forms utilisable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 utilisable。

definition_zh: 话语；发言；言辞；言语行为；（语言学的）话语句
definition_en: something that a person says out loud, spoken words, or the physical act of producing speech
core_image: 一句话从口中说出，落进空气里，成为一段可听见的声音
scene: 录音笔放在桌上，采访刚刚开始，老人低头想了一会儿才开口。Every utterance was later transcribed word by word.
sceneCN: 这里 utterance 是「说出的话语、言辞」（第 1 个义项：口头说出的某句话）；句意为每一句说过的话后来都被逐字转写下来。画面里是录音笔、访谈桌和一张写满字的稿纸。

pos.zh: 名词：话语；言论；言语行为；语言学中的话语句

collocations.zh: 说出；表达出（情感或想法）

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，加后缀 -ance 构成名词，义为「说出；发出（声音）」
由 utter 加 -able 再加否定前缀构成，义为「说不出口的；难以言表的」
较少见，由 utter（完全的）加 -less 与 -ly 构成，义为「无以言表地」

senses.title: Something said out loud
senses.definition: a word or remark that someone says aloud, especially one treated as a single thing that was said
senses.definitionCN: 某人说出口的词语或言论，尤指被当作一句完整话语看待的内容
senses.example: Every utterance in the interview was recorded and transcribed.
senses.exampleCN: 访谈中说的每句话都被录音并转写下来。
senses.why: The noun is built on utter, to let out with the voice, so an utterance is whatever the mouth lets out.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建立在动词 utter「用声音说出」之上，所以 utterance 就是嘴巴放出来的东西。

senses.title: The act of speaking
senses.definition: the action or fact of expressing something in speech rather than in writing
senses.definitionCN: 用口头言语而非书写表达某事的动作或事实
senses.example: The law protects the utterance of opinion in public places.
senses.exampleCN: 法律保护在公共场所发表意见的行为。
senses.why: The suffix -ance usually names an action or a state, so the word can point to the act of speaking, not only to the words.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ance 常表示动作或状态，因此这个词既能指话语，也能指「说」这个动作本身。

senses.title: A single unit of speech studied
senses.definition: in linguistics, a stretch of spoken language produced by one speaker on one occasion, studied together with its context
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中指说话人在一次场合中说出的一段口头语言，须连同语境一起研究
senses.example: The linguist compared each utterance with the gesture that came with it.
senses.exampleCN: 这位语言学家把每一句话与其伴随的手势作比较。
senses.why: Language study needed a countable unit of real speech, and the word that already meant something said was ready to carry that job.
senses.whyCN: 语言研究需要一个可数的真实言语单位，而这个词原本就表示「说出口的东西」，于是被拿来承担这一职能。

senses.title: Vocal sound as opposed to silence
senses.definition: a voiced sound or cry, often in contrast with silence
senses.definitionCN: 发出的声音或叫声，常与沉默相对
senses.example: Before the first utterance, the room had been totally silent.
senses.exampleCN: 在开口说出第一句话之前，屋里一片寂静。
senses.why: The verb utter also means to let out a sound, so the noun can cover any sound the voice makes, not only words.
senses.whyCN: 动词 utter 也有「发出声音」之义，所以这个词也涵盖嗓音发出的任何声响，而不只是词语。

senses.title: Give utterance to: express
senses.definition: in the phrase give utterance to, to express a feeling or idea in words
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 give utterance to，指把情感或想法用言语表达出来
senses.example: At last she gave utterance to the fear she had carried for years.
senses.exampleCN: 她终于说出了多年来藏在心里的恐惧。
senses.why: If an utterance is what comes out of the mouth, giving utterance is the act of letting it come out.
senses.whyCN: 如果 utterance 是从嘴里出来的东西，那么 give utterance 就是让它出来的动作。

senses.title: A brief remark
senses.definition: a short spoken remark, especially one that is quoted or remembered
senses.definitionCN: 简短的口头评论，尤指被引用或被记住的一句
senses.example: His only utterance on the topic was a single quiet word.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这个话题唯一的表态，只是轻轻说了一个词。
senses.why: Because the noun counts something said as one item, a very short remark can also be called an utterance.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词把「说过的话」当作一个计数单位，极短的一句评论也可以称为 utterance。

senses.title: Style of speech
senses.definition: formal or archaic use: the way a person speaks, including the manner and tone of their speech
senses.definitionCN: 正式或古雅的用法：一个人的说话方式，包括语气与措辞
senses.example: The old judge was known for the slow and careful utterance that filled his courtroom.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老法官以缓慢而谨慎的说话方式闻名，整个法庭都听得见。
senses.why: When people notice how something is said rather than which words are used, the noun shifts from the content to the manner.
senses.whyCN: 当人们注意到的是「怎么说」而不是「说了什么」时，这个词就从内容转向了方式。

intro.en: Utterance is an English noun built on the old English verb utter, from out plus a comparative ending, meaning to put out.
intro.cn: utterance 是英语中以后缀 -ance 构成的名词，基干是古英语动词 utter，来源于「out（出）」加比较级词尾，本义为「放出、推出」。

items.en: Utter comes from Old English ut, out, plus the comparative ending -er that also appears in inner and outer.
items.cn: utter 来自古英语 ut「出」，接比较级词尾 -er，与 inner、outer 同类的词尾一致。

items.en: The verb utteran means to put out, send out, or let out, at first of goods as well as of sounds.
items.cn: 动词 utteran 意为「放出、送出」，起初既用于货物，也用于声音。

items.en: The noun uttering or utterance forms on -ance and names the act of putting something forth in speech.
items.cn: 名词 uttering 与 utterance 以 -ance 构成，指把某事物用言语表达出来的行为。

items.en: Utterance is used for the spoken word itself as well as for the act of speaking.
items.cn: utterance 既指说话的行为，也开始指说出的话本身。

items.en: Linguistics adopts utterance as a technical unit of actual speech, and the everyday sense of a remark survives beside it.
items.cn: 语言学把 utterance 采纳为真实言语的技术单位，日常「言论」义则与它并存。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built from utter or from the same out-root; the near-meaning group gathers words for things said, ranging from a single remark to a formal statement.
note.cn: 形近组收由 utter 或同一「out（出）」来源构成的词；近义组收表示「说出的内容」的词，范围从一句话到正式声明不等。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to say or make a sound, and also an adjective meaning complete.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「说出、发出（声音）」；同时可作形容词，义为「完全的」。

entries.definition: An older noun naming the act of speaking, before the -ance form became usual.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的名词形式，指说话的行为，在加 -ance 的形式通行之前使用。

entries.definition: An adjective for what cannot be put into words, often a feeling too strong to speak.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「说不出口的、难以言表的」，多形容强到无法用言语表达的感受。

entries.definition: Something said, usually a short comment; more casual and less technical than utterance.
entries.definitionCN: 说出口的话，通常指简短的评论；比 utterance 更随意，也没有术语色彩。

entries.definition: A formal expression of facts or views, often issued in public.
entries.definitionCN: 对事实或观点的正式表达，常在公开场合发布。

entries.definition: The ability to speak, the act of speaking, or a prepared talk given to an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 说话的能力、说话的行为，或向听众作的演讲。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build on the real out-root of utter and on the phrases that the noun actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子建立在 utter 真实的「out（出）」词根，以及这个名词实际出现的搭配之上。

normal.en: Utter is out plus a comparative ending: to utter is to send a sound out of the mouth.
normal.cn: utter 是 out 加比较级词尾：说出口就是把声音从嘴里送出去。

normal.en: The suffix -ance is the same one that turns deliver into deliverance.
normal.cn: -ance 后缀与 deliver 变 deliverance 所用的是同一个。

normal.en: Give utterance to means to say what was held inside.
normal.cn: give utterance to 意为把藏在心里的话说出来。

normal.en: In linguistics each utterance is attached to a particular speaker, moment and place.
normal.cn: 在语言学里，每一句话都对应特定的说话人、时刻与场合。

normal.en: Compare remark: a remark is casual, an utterance is the speech event itself.
normal.cn: 对比 remark：remark 是随口的评论，utterance 更接近一次言语事件本身。

abstract.en: Picture smoke leaving a mouth: whatever the mouth lets out is an utterance.
abstract.cn: 想象一口气从嘴边飘出去：嘴里放出来的东西就是 utterance。

abstract.en: Keep the edge of the road in sight: it is not too sharp on this side, and it stays ut with me.
abstract.cn: 记忆要保留一个清楚的路标：这一侧不算太窄，它就「在」我心里。

abstract.en: One spoken sentence, one dot: a line of dots is a conversation.
abstract.cn: 一句话就是一个点：一串点连起来就是一场对话。

examples.en: Her calm utterances at the meeting impressed the board.
examples.cn: 她在会上从容的发言让董事会印象深刻。

examples.en: Analysts studied recorded utterances to understand regional speech.
examples.cn: 分析人员研究录下来的话语，以了解地方口音的特点。

examples.en: Only one utterance was heard before the microphone went silent.
examples.cn: 麦克风静音之前，只听到一句话被说了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊特问」——先发出「啊」的一声，再特地问一句，就是说出话；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ut「出」加比较级词尾 -er 构成 utter「放出、说出」；再加后缀 -ance 构成 utterance。词根与 inner、outer 的 -er 同源，关系明白，无需重构。

sensesIntro.en: Utterance starts from something let out of the mouth and spreads: first a spoken remark, then the act of speaking, then the linguist unit, then a sound, a set phrase, a short item, and finally a person speech style.
sensesIntro.cn: utterance 从「从嘴里放出来的东西」出发一路铺开：先是说出的话，再是说话的动作，然后是语言学的单位、发出的声音、固定短语、简短言论，最后是个人说话的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoken line leaves the mouth and hangs in the air as a sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话从口中说出，停在空气里成为声音。

branches.en: THE CONTENT: a remark of any length that has been said out loud.
branches.cn: 内容线：长短不论，凡被说出口的言论都是 utterance。

branches.en: THE ACT: saying something itself, especially the set phrase give utterance to.
branches.cn: 动作线：指「说」这个行为，尤其是固定短语 give utterance to。

branches.en: THE STUDY: a countable unit of real speech in linguistics.
branches.cn: 研究线：语言学中可计数的真实言语单位。

branches.en: THE SOUND: any voice coming out, even without words.
branches.cn: 声音线：嗓音发出的任何声响，甚至可以没有词语。

branches.en: THE MANNER: how a person speaks, rather than what is said.
branches.cn: 方式线：说的是一个人的说话方式，而不是说出的内容。

intro.en: Utterance is a short English stem, utter, plus the common noun suffix -ance, with a small family built around it.
intro.cn: utterance 由简短的英语词干 utter 加常见名词后缀 -ance 构成，周围还有一小族同源词。

latinIntro.en: This word is native English; its out-root is older than Latin borrowings, so Latin forms are shown only for comparison.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，其「出」的词根比拉丁语借词更早，下面的拉丁语形式只用于对照说明。

items.example: The old verb meant to send something out of the hands.
items.exampleCN: 这个古动词本义是把东西从手里送出去。

items.example: Out is the first half of utter.
items.exampleCN: out 是 utter 的前半部分。

items.example: The same ending appears in outer.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾也出现在 outer 中。

items.example: The suffix turns utter into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 utter 变成名词。

items.meaning: to say or make a sound
items.example: The verb survives on its own.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词至今独立使用。

items.example: The prefix negates the adjective built on utter.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀对由 utter 构成的形容词加以否定。

items.example: It combines with un- to form unutterable.
items.exampleCN: 它与 un- 结合构成 unutterable。

items.meaning: too strong to be put into words
items.meaningCN: 说不出口的；难以言表的
items.example: Unutterable describes feelings beyond words.
items.exampleCN: unutterable 形容难以言说的感受。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 说出；宣布（仅供对照，并非本词来源）

definition_zh: 完全地；彻底地；十足地
definition_en: completely and without any doubt, used for emphasis before a strong word
core_image: 一只杯子一直倒到杯沿，最后一滴也倒进去，一滴不剩
scene: 厨房里灯光很暗，桌上的饭菜已经凉透，主人却还在门口等着。The evening was utterly ruined when the guests never arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 utterly 是「彻底地、完全地」（第 1 个义项：把程度推到尽头）；句意为客人始终没来，整个晚上彻底毁了。画面里有冷掉的饭菜、暗掉的灯和一个守着门的人。

pos.zh: 副词：完全地；彻底地；十足地（用于强化语气）

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 得到形容词，义为「完全的；彻底的」，如 utter failure
由 utter 加 -ness 构成，义为「完全；彻底」，虽少见但见诸词典

senses.title: Completely, to the last degree
senses.definition: fully and completely, with nothing held back or left over
senses.definitionCN: 彻底而完全，没有任何保留或剩余
senses.example: By midnight the village was utterly quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 到午夜时，村子里彻底安静了下来。
senses.why: Utter as an adjective means complete or absolute, and -ly turns that absolute limit into an adverb of degree.
senses.whyCN: utter 作形容词时意为「完全的、绝对的」，加 -ly 后把这个「到底」的极限变成程度副词。

senses.title: Emphasising a strong judgement
senses.definition: used before a strong adjective to add force, as in utterly disastrous or utterly ridiculous
senses.definitionCN: 放在强烈的形容词前加强语气，如 utterly disastrous「灾难性的」、utterly ridiculous「荒谬透顶的」
senses.example: The plan was utterly ridiculous from the very first page.
senses.exampleCN: 这份方案从第一页起就荒谬透顶。
senses.why: The word works like the final blow: it pushes a word that is already strong all the way to its edge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词像最后一击：把本已强烈的词一路推到它的极限。

senses.title: In a state of failure or ruin
senses.definition: used in phrases such as utterly failed or utterly ruined, where a failure or loss is total
senses.definitionCN: 用于 utterly failed、utterly ruined 等说法中，表示失败或损失是百分百的
senses.example: The negotiations utterly failed and the strike went ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判彻底失败，罢工照旧举行。
senses.why: A total defeat has no part left standing; the adverb marks that nothing survived the collapse.
senses.whyCN: 彻底的失败不会留下任何还站得住的部分；这个副词标记出崩塌中无一幸存。

senses.title: In a different way altogether
senses.definition: used with unlike, different or other words to mean in no way similar
senses.definitionCN: 与 unlike、different 等词连用，表示毫无相似之处
senses.example: The twin brothers look alike but act utterly differently.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎兄弟长得很像，处事方式却截然不同。
senses.why: Two things can be compared; utterly says the comparison ends in zero overlap.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西可以被比较；utterly 宣告这场比较的重叠为零。

senses.title: A complete personal state
senses.titleCN: 身心完全处于某种状态
senses.definition: used with states such as exhausted, alone or helpless to show that the state fills the person
senses.definitionCN: 与 exhausted、alone、helpless 等状态词连用，表示这种状态占满了整个人
senses.example: After the marathon she was utterly exhausted and could hardly speak.
senses.exampleCN: 跑完马拉松后，她彻底累垮了，几乎说不出话。
senses.why: A feeling that fills a whole person leaves no corner of energy for anything else.
senses.whyCN: 充满整个人的感受不会在角落留下任何余力去做别的事。

senses.title: Totally in belief or agreement
senses.definition: used with convinced, certain or persuaded to mean without the slightest doubt
senses.definitionCN: 与 convinced、certain 等词连用，表示没有一丝疑虑
senses.example: The judge was utterly convinced that the witness was honest.
senses.exampleCN: 法官完全相信证人是诚实的。
senses.why: Doubt is a space; utterly closes that space so that nothing is left open.
senses.whyCN: 怀疑是一种空隙；utterly 把这个空隙关紧，不留下任何开口。

senses.title: As a refusal or denial
senses.titleCN: 断然；坚决地（常用于否定）
senses.definition: used with deny or refuse to make the rejection flat and complete
senses.definitionCN: 与 deny、refuse 连用，使拒绝或否认显得干脆利落、毫无余地
senses.example: He utterly denied ever meeting the witness.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚决否认曾见过这名证人。
senses.why: To refuse utterly is to refuse right to the end, with no partial answer offered.
senses.whyCN: utterly refuse 就是拒绝到底，不给出任何折中的答复。

intro.en: Utterly is the adverb of utter, a word that began as a comparison of out and split into an outer and an inner meaning.
intro.cn: utterly 是 utter 的副词形式，而 utter 本由 out 的比较级构成，后来分出了「向外」和「到底」两层意思。

items.en: Utter descends from ut, out, with the comparative ending -er, literally meaning further out.
items.cn: utter 由 ut「出」加比较级词尾 -er 构成，字面义为「更往外」。

items.en: The adjective uttera is used for the outer or furthest part, as in the uttermost edge.
items.cn: 形容词 uttera 用于表示「外面的、最远的」部分，如 uttermost「最边缘的」。

items.en: The sense shifts from the furthest edge to the furthest point of a quality, giving complete or absolute.
items.cn: 词义从「最边缘的位置」转向「某种性质的最远点」，于是有了「完全的、绝对的」之义。

items.en: The adverb utterly appears in the modern sense, used before strong words to mean completely.
items.cn: 副词 utterly 以现代的「完全」义出现，多放在强烈的词前加强语气。

items.en: Utterly keeps to emphatic use; in formal writing and speech it has become rather literary.
items.cn: utterly 专用于强调，在正式书面语与演讲中带有一定的文学色彩。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the utter family; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of completeness and force that differ in tone and collocation.
note.cn: 形近组收 utter 一族的形式；近义组收表示「完全、强烈」的副词，彼此在语气与搭配上不同。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning complete or absolute, as in utter silence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「完全的、绝对的」，如 utter silence「一片寂静」。

entries.definition: A form of the verb utter, meaning saying a word aloud; it looks related but does not mean completely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词 utter 的形式，义为「说出」，虽与 utterly 同形近，却与「完全」义无关。

entries.definition: The rare noun for the quality of being complete, formed with -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 少见的名词形式，义为「完全、极致」，由 utter 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: To the full extent; the plainest and most neutral of these adverbs.
entries.definitionCN: 完全地，是这几个副词中最朴素、最中性的一个。

entries.definition: As a whole, especially in speech; common with ruined, wrong and different.
entries.definitionCN: 整体地、完全地，口语中很常见，常与 ruined、wrong、different 连用。

entries.definition: Without limit or condition; forceful and often used in emphatic replies.
entries.definitionCN: 绝对地、无条件地，语气强，常用于强调性的回答中。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real out-root of utter and the way the adverb behaves with strong words.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子利用 utter 真实的「出」词根，以及这个副词与强烈词语搭配时的特点。

normal.en: Utter is out plus -er: utterly means pushed all the way out, to the end.
normal.cn: utter 是 out 加 -er：utterly 意为一路推到最外面、推到尽头。

normal.en: Utter means complete as an adjective, and -ly makes it an adverb of degree.
normal.cn: utter 作形容词意为「完全的」，加 -ly 就成了表示程度的副词。

normal.en: Utterly pairs with strong adjectives: utterly exhausted, utterly ridiculous.
normal.cn: utterly 常与强烈的形容词搭配：utterly exhausted、utterly ridiculous。

normal.en: In ordinary conversation totally and completely are more common; utterly sounds slightly formal or literary.
normal.cn: 日常对话里 totally、completely 更常用；utterly 听起来稍正式，带文学味。

normal.en: The adjective form is just utter: an utter failure is a failure that leaves nothing standing.
normal.cn: 形容词形式就是 utter：an utter failure 指败得什么都不剩的失败。

abstract.en: Picture a cup filled to the very brim: one more drop and it spills, and nothing is held back.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子倒到杯沿：再一滴就溢出，一点都没保留。

abstract.en: Keep the edge of the road in sight again: the line spells how far it can go, all the way out on my side.
abstract.cn: 再看一眼路边的边线：这条线标出能走多远，一路延伸到我这侧的最外边。

abstract.en: Hear the sound of something snapping shut with a click: that is doubt being closed for good.
abstract.cn: 听见某物咔哒一声合上的声音：那就是疑虑被彻底关死的声音。

examples.en: The committee was utterly convinced by the new evidence.
examples.cn: 新证据让委员会完全信服。

examples.en: She was utterly exhausted after the third night shift.
examples.cn: 连续第三个夜班之后，她彻底累垮了。

examples.en: Their answers to the same question were utterly different.
examples.cn: 他们对同一个问题的回答截然不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿特利」——一口气「特」别「厉」害地推到到底，就是彻底；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: utter + -ly。utter 由古英语 ut「出」加比较级词尾 -er 构成，先指「外面的、最远的」，后引申为「完全的、绝对的」；副词 utterly 即由此而来。

sensesIntro.en: Utterly always marks a limit reached: a state that is complete, a judgement pushed to its edge, a failure with nothing left, a difference with no overlap, a person wholly filled, a belief without doubt, or a refusal given to the end.
sensesIntro.cn: utterly 始终标记「达到极限」：完全的状态、被推到顶点的判断、不剩一点的失败、毫无重叠的差异、占满一个人的感受、没有疑虑的相信，以及拒绝到底的表态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup is filled to the brim, with the last drop still on its way.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子倒到杯沿，最后一滴还在路上。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: a state filled to the top, like a tired body or a silent village.
branches.cn: 极限线：被填满的状态，比如疲惫不堪的身体或一片寂静的村子。

branches.en: THE FORCE: added to a strong word to push it to its edge.
branches.cn: 力度线：加在强烈词语前，把它推到极限。

branches.en: THE RUIN: a failure or loss so total that nothing survives.
branches.cn: 崩塌线：失败或损失彻底到无一幸存。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: a difference with zero overlap.
branches.cn: 对比线：差异大到毫无重叠。

branches.en: THE CLOSURE: doubt or refusal closed tight, with no room left open.
branches.cn: 封闭线：疑虑或拒绝被关得严严实实，不留余地。

intro.en: Utterly is the adjective utter plus the very common adverbial suffix -ly; the base itself is an old out-word.
intro.cn: utterly 是形容词 utter 加极常见的副词后缀 -ly 构成，基干本身是古老的「出」类词。

latinIntro.en: This word is native English and has no Latin parts; the forms below are Latin words that English speakers used for similar ideas.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，没有拉丁语构件；下面列出的拉丁语词只是表达相近概念时使用的对照形式。

items.example: The adjective says a quality has reached its end.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词表示某种性质已到尽头。

items.example: The suffix turns utter into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 utter 变成副词。

items.example: Out lies behind the first syllable.
items.exampleCN: out 正是第一个音节背后的来源。

items.example: The ending made out into a comparison.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 out 变成了比较形式。

items.example: Outer shows the same ending at work.
items.exampleCN: outer 展示了同一个词尾的用法。

items.example: Utmost keeps the furthest-point image.
items.exampleCN: utmost 保留了「最远那一点」的意象。

items.example: The suffix forms the rare noun utterness.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成少见名词 utterness。

items.example: It builds uttermost from utter.
items.exampleCN: 它由 utter 构成 uttermost。
