definition_zh: 空缺；（旅馆的）空房；空职；空位；空虚
definition_en: an unfilled job, an unoccupied room, or a space that is empty and waiting to be filled
core_image: 一栋楼里熄了灯的那扇窗，房间里空着，正等着人搬进来
scene: 前台翻着厚厚的登记册，外面下着小雨，客人排着队等房间。Only one room vacancy was left for the whole weekend.
sceneCN: 这里 vacancy 是「空房」（第 2 个义项：旅馆里尚未租出的房间）；句意为整个周末只剩下一间空房。画面里有登记册、前台灯和门外排队的客人。

pos.zh: 名词：空缺；空职；空房；空位；空虚

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词根 vac- 加 -ant 构成，义为「空的；空缺的；无人居住的」
同词根加动词后缀，义为「腾出；搬出；辞去」
拉丁语 e-（出）加 vac- 构成，义为「疏散；撤离；排空」
同词根的拉丁中性名词，义为「真空；真空吸尘器」

senses.title: An unfilled job
senses.definition: a job or position that is not filled because the person who held it has left
senses.definitionCN: 因原任职者离开而尚未补上的工作岗位
senses.example: The hospital advertised three vacancies for night nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院公开招聘三个夜班护士的空缺。
senses.why: Vacare means to be empty, and modern offices call an empty post a vacancy because the seat stands unfilled.
senses.whyCN: vacare 意为「空着」，现代职场把空着的岗位称作 vacancy，只因座位还没有人坐。

senses.title: An unoccupied hotel room
senses.definition: a room in a hotel or other place of lodging that has no guest and is free to let
senses.definitionCN: 旅馆或住宿处尚未住客、可以出租的房间
senses.example: The sign by the door said there were no vacancies.
senses.exampleCN: 门边的告示上写着客满。
senses.why: A lodging keeps the oldest and most concrete image of emptiness: a room with the light off and the key still on its hook.
senses.whyCN: 住宿行业保留了这个词最古老也最具体的「空」：灯没开、钥匙还挂在钩上的房间。

senses.title: A blank space in a form or page
senses.definition: an empty space left in a form, page or surface for something to be written or placed later
senses.definitionCN: 表格、页面或平面上留出来、待填写的空白处
senses.example: Fill the vacancy in the form with your passport number.
senses.exampleCN: 请在表格的空白处填上护照号码。
senses.why: Any empty place that waits for a filler is a vacancy, whether it is a room, a seat, or a blank line.
senses.whyCN: 任何等着被填入的空处都是 vacancy，无论是房间、座位，还是一行空白。

senses.title: A sense of inner emptiness
senses.definition: a feeling of being empty or without purpose, often in literary description
senses.definitionCN: 感到空荡、没有目标的心境，多用于文学描写
senses.example: After the children left home, he felt a strange vacancy in his days.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们离家之后，他感到日子里有种说不出的空。
senses.why: The same emptiness moves inside a person: what used to be filled now has nothing to fill it.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「空」移到了人的内心：原本被填满的地方如今没有什么来填。

senses.title: Emptiness of a look or face
senses.definition: a blank or unresponsive expression, in which no thought or feeling shows
senses.definitionCN: 面无表情、毫无反应的样子，显不出任何想法或情绪
senses.example: There was a vacancy in his eyes as he watched the news.
senses.exampleCN: 他看新闻时，眼神里一片空洞。
senses.why: A face whose expression has gone away is empty before others, and the word reaches that blank surface too.
senses.whyCN: 神情褪去的脸在别人眼里就是空的，这个词也延伸到了这片空白上。

senses.title: Unoccupied land or property
senses.definition: a house, office or plot of land that is empty and not in use, as measured by property statistics
senses.definitionCN: 空着、未使用的住宅、办公室或土地，常以数据统计加以衡量
senses.example: Long-term vacancies have pushed down shop rents in the old district.
senses.exampleCN: 长期空置拉低了老城区的商铺租金。
senses.why: Property records count empty buildings with the same word used for an empty room, only on a larger scale.
senses.whyCN: 房产记录用与空房间相同的词来统计空置的楼房，只是尺度更大。

senses.title: An opening in a court or team
senses.definition: an open place in a sports team, a court or an organised group where a member is needed
senses.definitionCN: 体育队、球场或组织中需要成员补上的名额
senses.example: The injury of the striker left a vacancy in the starting line-up.
senses.exampleCN: 前锋受伤后，首发阵容里出现了一个空缺。
senses.why: A team is also a set of filled places, and when one member goes a hole appears where a player used to stand.
senses.whyCN: 一支球队同样是一组填满的位置；一名队员离开后，原来的位置上就出现了一个洞。

senses.title: Freedom from work or occupation
senses.definition: formal or literary use: free time in which a person has nothing to occupy them
senses.definitionCN: 正式或文学用法：没有工作可做的空闲时间
senses.example: In leisure hours he would read whatever came to hand.
senses.exampleCN: 有了闲暇，他抓到什么书就读什么书。
senses.why: The oldest Latin sense was simply being unoccupied, so time itself could be spoken of as empty.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的拉丁义就是「闲着、无事」，所以时间本身也能被说成是空的。

intro.en: Vacancy comes from Latin vacare, to be empty or unoccupied, through the adjective vacans and the medieval noun vacantia.
intro.cn: vacancy 来自拉丁语 vacare「空着、闲着」，经由形容词 vacans 与中世纪的 vacantia 进入英语。

items.en: The root *h₁weh₂-, meaning to leave or to be empty, is reconstructed; the deeper connection with wane is debated.
items.cn: *h₁weh₂-「留下、空出」属于重构形式；与 wane「减少」是否有更深联系，学界尚有争议。

items.en: Vacare means to be empty, to be free from work or to be unoccupied.
items.cn: vacare 意为「空着、有空、无工作」。

items.en: The present participle vacans means being empty or unoccupied, and gives English vacant.
items.cn: 现在分词 vacans 意为「空着的、无人的」，英语的 vacant 即由此而来。

items.en: Medieval and legal Latin vacantia names the state of being empty, especially of a post or a property.
items.cn: 中世纪及法律拉丁语 vacantia 指「空缺、空置状态」，尤其用于职位或产业。

items.en: English borrows vacancy first for a vacant post, then extends it to rooms, forms and the mind.
items.cn: 英语最早把 vacancy 用于空缺职位，随后扩展到房间、表格与内心。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin root vac-; the near-meaning group gathers words for empty places and openings with slightly different uses.
note.cn: 形近组收以拉丁词根 vac- 构成的词；近义组收表示「空处、空缺」的词，用法略有区别。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a seat, room or look that is empty or shows nothing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容座位、房间是空的，或神情空洞。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to leave a room, seat or post so that it becomes empty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「腾出、搬出、辞去」，使房间或位置变空。

entries.definition: A space with no matter in it, or a tool that cleans by suction; from the same empty root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「真空」或「真空吸尘器」，出自同一「空」词根。

entries.definition: A chance or place that is open to someone, often used for jobs like vacancy.
entries.definitionCN: 向人开放的岗位或机会，谈工作时与 vacancy 相近。

entries.definition: A narrow break or an unfilled space between two things.
entries.definitionCN: 两物之间的缝隙或未填满的空档。

entries.definition: A space on a page left empty for writing, close to the form sense of vacancy.
entries.definitionCN: 页面上留待填写的空格，与 vacancy 的表格空白义相近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real vac- root, the Latin verb vacare, and the phrases that vacancy actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子利用真实的 vac- 词根、拉丁语动词 vacare，以及 vacancy 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Vacare means to be empty: a vacancy is an empty place that waits for someone.
normal.cn: vacare 意为「空着」：vacancy 就是一个等着人来的空位。

normal.en: The same root gives vacant, vacate and vacuum; all of them are about emptiness.
normal.cn: 同一词根生出 vacant、vacate、vacuum，它们都与「空」有关。

normal.en: A hotel puts up the sign no vacancies when every room is taken.
normal.cn: 旅馆房间全部住满时会挂出 no vacancies 的告示。

normal.en: Hiring managers fill a vacancy; the word keeps the image of a hole in a team.
normal.cn: 招聘经理会 fill a vacancy：这个词保留了「队伍里一个洞」的意象。

normal.en: Compare vacant: vacant describes the thing that is empty, vacancy names the emptiness itself.
normal.cn: 对比 vacant：vacant 形容空着的东西，vacancy 指那个「空」本身。

abstract.en: Picture a dark window among lit ones in an apartment block: that single window is the vacancy.
abstract.cn: 想象公寓楼里一排亮着的窗中有一扇黑着的：那一扇窗就是 vacancy。

abstract.en: Keep the empty post in sight: a board marked free, and nobody sitting under it yet.
abstract.cn: 记住那个空着的岗位：一块写着「空」的牌子，下面还没有人坐。

abstract.en: Think of a tea cup set upside down on a tray: it holds nothing, and it waits for tea.
abstract.cn: 想一只倒扣在托盘上的茶杯：里面什么都没有，正等着茶。

examples.en: There is a vacancy in the marketing team for a junior designer.
examples.cn: 市场部有一个初级设计师的空缺。

examples.en: The motel had vacancies even in the middle of summer.
examples.cn: 即使在盛夏，这家汽车旅馆也还有空房。

examples.en: Officials are worried about the rising vacancy rate in city centre offices.
examples.cn: 官员们担心市中心写字楼的空置率不断上升。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为看西」——为看西边的月亮，房间一直空着；只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vacare「空着、闲着」→ 现在分词 vacans「空着的」（英语 vacant）→ 中世纪 vacantia「空缺状态」→ 英语 vacancy。词根 *h₁weh₂-「留下、空出」为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Vacancy begins with a simple empty space and grows into a missing worker, a free room, a blank line, an inner emptiness, a blank face, an unused building, an open place in a team, and even empty time.
sensesIntro.cn: vacancy 从一个简单的空处出发，长成缺失的人手、空着的房间、待填的空白、内心的空荡、木然的神情、闲置的楼房、队伍里的空位，乃至空出来的时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one dark window in a block of lit windows, with a room left empty inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栋楼里只有一扇窗黑着，里面的房间空着。

branches.en: THE PLACE: a room or a building with nobody inside, counted by hosts and by property records.
branches.cn: 场所线：里面没人的房间或楼房，既由店主统计，也进入房产记录。

branches.en: THE POST: a place in a team or a staff list where a person is missing.
branches.cn: 岗位线：球队或员工名单里缺人的那个位置。

branches.en: THE FORM: a blank space on paper that waits to be written in.
branches.cn: 表格线：纸上留待书写的一块空白。

branches.en: THE MIND: emptiness inside a person, or a face with no expression on it.
branches.cn: 内心线：人心里的一片空，或脸上没有任何表情的木然。

branches.en: THE TIME: hours without work, described in older and literary writing.
branches.cn: 时间线：没有工作的时段，见于较早与文学性的文字。

intro.en: Vacancy rests on the Latin root vac-, with the noun suffix -ancy; a whole family of words for emptiness gathers around it.
intro.cn: vacancy 建立在拉丁词根 vac- 之上，后接名词后缀 -ancy；周围聚集了一整族表示「空」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vacare is well recorded, and the adjective vacans and the medieval noun vacantia follow from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vacare 有可靠的文献记录，其形容词 vacans 与中世纪名词 vacantia 都由它产生。

items.example: The root carries the idea of something left empty.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载着「被空出来」的意思。

items.example: The verb is the direct ancestor.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是直接的祖先词。

items.example: The suffix names the state of being empty.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀表示「空着」的状态。

items.example: It forms the adjective vacant.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词 vacant。

items.example: It turns the root into the verb vacate.
items.exampleCN: 它把词根变成动词 vacate。

items.example: E- plus vac- forms evacuate, to empty out.
items.exampleCN: e- 加 vac- 构成 evacuate，意为「排空、撤出」。

items.example: It forms vacuous, meaning empty of thought.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 vacuous，意为「空洞无物的」。

items.example: It builds vacuity from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 它由同一词根构成 vacuity「空洞」。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 闲暇；空闲（即 vacare 作「闲着」讲的一面）

definition_zh: （决定、立场）举棋不定；动摇；来回摇摆
definition_en: to keep changing your mind or position between two choices and fail to settle on one
core_image: 一个人站在两条岔路口，左脚迈出又收回，身子在两边之间来回晃
scene: 选专业那几天，他上午说要学建筑，下午又说想读历史，晚上又把表格合上不肯提交。He vacillated between architecture and history for a week.
sceneCN: 这里 vacillate 是「举棋不定」（第 1 个义项：在两种选择之间反复改主意）；句意：他在建筑和历史之间摇摆了整整一周。

pos.zh: 举棋不定；动摇；（在两者之间）摇摆不定

collocations.zh: 在两个选择之间摇摆不定

derivatives.zh: 由 vacillate 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「踌躇；摇摆不定」
由现在分词转成的形容词，义为「犹豫不决的；摇摆不定的」
由动词加 -or 构成，义为「犹豫不决的人」，较少使用
由名词词干加 -ory 构成，义为「摇摆的；踌躇的」，属书面语

senses.title: To keep changing between choices
senses.definition: to swing back and forth between two possible choices without settling on either
senses.definitionCN: 在两个可能的选择之间来回变动，始终定不下来
senses.example: She vacillated between the two job offers for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 她在那两个工作机会之间犹豫了整整一个月。
senses.why: Latin vacillare means to sway or totter, like a body losing its balance, so a mind that cannot stand still between choices borrows the picture of a rocking body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vacillare 意为「摇晃、摇晃欲倒」，身体失去平衡的画面被借去形容在两种选择之间站不稳的头脑。

senses.title: A position that keeps shifting
senses.definition: to change a stated position, opinion, or policy repeatedly, especially in public life
senses.definitionCN: 反复改变公开表明的立场、意见或政策，尤见于公众事务
senses.example: The minister vacillated on the tax plan until the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 这位部长直到投票前一直在税改方案上摇摆。
senses.why: Old writers first used the verb for a speaker whose words swayed, and modern public language still applies it to an office holder who will not hold a line.
senses.whyCN: 早期作者先用这个词形容说话摇摆的人，现代公共话语则沿用它在官职人物身上，指责其不能坚持立场。

senses.title: Physical swaying in an older register
senses.definition: to move unsteadily from side to side, a use mostly found in older writing
senses.definitionCN: 左右不稳地晃动，主要用于旧式书面语
senses.example: The old lamp vacillated whenever a cart passed below.
senses.exampleCN: 每当下面有马车经过，那盏旧灯便摇晃起来。
senses.why: The Latin verb named a physical sway before it named a mental one, and a few old sentences keep the original body-based sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词先指身体晃动，后指心中摇摆；这类旧句子把最初基于身体的含义保留了下来。

intro.en: Vacillate comes from Latin vacillare, to sway or totter, and reached English in the sixteenth century as a word for a mind that will not stand firm.
intro.cn: vacillate 来自拉丁语 vacillare（摇晃、站立不稳），十六世纪进入英语，指定不下来的头脑。

items.en: Vacillare means to sway, totter, or be unsteady on the feet.
items.cn: vacillare 意为摇晃、踉跄、站不稳。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain, though some connect it with a root meaning to waver.
items.cn: 更早的来源不确定，有说法把它与表示「摇动」的词根联系起来。

items.en: English borrows the verb and applies it first to hesitant speech and thought.
items.cn: 英语借入该动词，最初用于犹豫的言辞和思想。

items.en: Writers extend it to public positions, so a politician or a policy can vacillate.
items.cn: 作家把用法扩展到公开立场，于是政客和政策也能「摇摆」。

items.en: Modern English keeps the formal tone and pairs the verb mainly with between, over, and on.
items.cn: 现代英语保留书面语色彩，常与 between、over、on 搭配。

note.en: Vacillate is the formal verb of indecision, close to its own word family and to waver, fluctuate, and hesitate.
note.cn: vacillate 是表示犹豫不决的正式动词，与自己的词族以及 waver、fluctuate、hesitate 相邻。

entries.definition: the act of being unable to decide
unable to decide and likely to change
entries.definitionCN: 犹豫不决的；摇摆不定的

entries.definition: marked by wavering
to become unsteady in purpose or belief
to rise and fall or change irregularly
to pause before acting or deciding

normalIntro.en: Vacillate is the formal word for a mind that keeps rocking from one choice to the other.
normalIntro.cn: vacillate 是形容头脑在两种选择之间来回摇晃的正式用词。

normal.en: The base is Latin vacillare, to sway, so the verb pictures a body that cannot stand still.
normal.cn: 词基是拉丁语 vacillare（摇晃），所以这个动词描绘的是站不稳的身体。

normal.en: The noun vacillation names the swinging, and the adjective vacillating names the person who swings.
normal.cn: 名词 vacillation 指这种摇摆，形容词 vacillating 指摇摆的人。

normal.en: The usual pattern is vacillate between two things, as in between two offers.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 vacillate between 两样东西，例如在两个录用通知之间。

normal.en: Over and on take a single topic, as in vacillate over the budget.
normal.cn: over 和 on 后面接单一话题，例如在预算上犹豫。

normal.en: Compare waver: waver is more literary and can describe light or hope, while vacillate keeps to decisions and positions.
normal.cn: 对比 waver：waver 更文学化，也能形容光和希望；vacillate 专指决定与立场。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose left foot steps out and then pulls back before the right foot moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人左脚迈出去又缩回来，右脚迟迟不动。

abstract.en: Think of a weather vane turning each time the wind changes direction.
abstract.cn: 想象风向标每换一次风向就转一回。

abstract.en: See a lamp swaying on its cord as a cart rattles past below.
abstract.cn: 看见一盏灯在灯绳上摇，因为下面有马车颠过。

examples.en: The committee vacillated between two designs for months.
examples.cn: 委员会在两个设计方案之间犹豫了好几个月。

examples.en: Do not vacillate on this point, because the deadline is near.
examples.cn: 不要在这点上动摇，截止日期就在眼前。

examples.en: Her latest vacillation surprised even close friends.
examples.cn: 她最近的这次反复连好友都觉得意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哇，谁来推」——一句「哇，谁来推一下」，人就左右摇晃起来，正好对上一个拿不定主意、来回摇摆的人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vacillare（摇晃、站不稳）→ 拉丁语 vacillatio（摇摆）→ 英语 vacillate，核心义「在两种选择之间站不稳」。

sensesIntro.en: Vacillate starts with a mind that keeps changing between choices, extends to a public position that keeps shifting, and survives in older writing with its literal sense of physical swaying.
sensesIntro.cn: vacillate 先指在两种选择之间不断改主意的头脑，再扩展到反复变动的公开立场，最后在旧式书面语中保留「身体摇晃」的本义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person whose feet keep lifting and settling at a fork in the road.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在岔路口的人，双脚反复抬起又落下。

branches.en: The everyday sense is a mind that will not settle between two choices.
branches.cn: 日常义项是头脑在两个选择之间定不下来。

branches.en: Public figures who keep changing policy are said to vacillate.
branches.cn: 政策反复变的公众人物被称为摇摆不定。

branches.en: The oldest use described a body that sways, now mostly literary.
branches.cn: 最早的用法描述摇晃的身体，如今多见于文学作品。

branches.en: Indecision and a shifting standpoint share the picture of a thing that will not hold its line.
branches.cn: 犹豫与立场多变共享同一个画面：一样东西守不住自己的线。

branches.en: An older sense of physical swaying explains the mental sense of swinging back and forth.
branches.cn: 旧义中身体的摇晃，解释了心中来回摆动的义项。

intro.en: Vacillate is a Latin verb borrowed whole, and English builds vacillation, vacillating, vacillator, and vacillatory around the same stem.
intro.cn: vacillate 是从拉丁语整体借入的动词，英语围绕同一词干构成 vacillation、vacillating、vacillator 与 vacillatory。

latinIntro.en: Latin vacillare means to sway, and its gerund-based forms gave English the noun and adjective of wavering.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vacillare 意为摇晃，其动名词类形式为英语提供了表示摇摆的名词与形容词。

items.example: Vacillare gives the swaying picture behind the verb.
items.exampleCN: vacillare 提供了这个动词背后的摇晃画面。

items.example: The participle stem leads to English adjective forms.
items.exampleCN: 分词词干引出了英语的形容词形式。

items.example: Vacillatio is the model for the English noun.
items.exampleCN: vacillatio 是英语名词的模型。

items.example: The ending -ate marks the borrowed Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 标记借入的拉丁动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ion forms vacillation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 vacillation。

items.meaning: the act or a continuing quality
items.meaningCN: 表示行为或持续特性的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms vacillating.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 vacillating。

items.example: The suffix -or forms vacillator.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 vacillator。

items.meaningCN: 表示倾向的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ory forms vacillatory.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ory 构成 vacillatory。

items.example: A vacillating leader loses trust.
items.exampleCN: 摇摆不定的领导者会失去信任。

definition_zh: 空虚；空洞；空洞无物的言论或内容；缺乏思考的状态
definition_en: a total lack of serious content, interest, or thought, often in a person or in speech
core_image: 一只薄薄的玻璃杯空着放在桌上，倒扣起来能听见回声，敲一下还嗡嗡作响
scene: 那场大会发言从头到尾都是口号，既没有数据也没有方案，坐在台下的听众面面相觑。The speech was applauded and then forgotten for its vacuity.
sceneCN: 这里 vacuity 是「空洞无物」（第 1 个义项：缺少实质内容的言论或状态）；句意：那场演讲除了空洞几乎一无所有，事后人们只是鼓掌便忘掉了。

pos.zh: 空虚；（言论、作品的）空洞无物；迟钝麻木的状态

derivatives.zh: 与 vacuity 同源，源自拉丁语 vacuus（空的），义为「空洞的；无所用心的」
由 vacuous 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「空洞地；茫然地」
由前缀 e-（出）加拉丁语 vacuus 构成，义为「撤离；排空」
由 vacuous 加 -ness 构成，义为「空洞；茫然」，与 vacuity 近义

senses.title: Emptiness of thought or content
senses.titleCN: 空洞无物；（言论、作品的）空虚内容
senses.definition: a complete absence of meaning, substance, or serious thought in what is said or made
senses.definitionCN: 所说或所做之事完全缺乏意义、实质或认真思考
senses.example: Critics dismissed the film for its moral vacuity.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家批评这部电影在道义上一片空洞，不值一提。
senses.why: Latin vacuus means empty, and a text that holds nothing useful is like a vessel with nothing in it, so the quality of being empty became the absence of substance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vacuus 意为「空的」，没有什么东西可装的文本就像空容器，于是「空」这一性质自然转为「缺乏实质」。

senses.title: A blank, unthinking look
senses.definition: an empty or unthinking expression, the look of a mind that is not engaged
senses.definitionCN: 空洞、不动脑子的表情，像心思根本没在场的眼神
senses.example: There was a strange vacuity in his eyes after the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到那个消息后，他眼里有一种奇怪的茫然。
senses.why: The face can look like an empty room, and an earlier English sense of being empty or void supported this use of the word for a person with nothing behind the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 脸庞可以像一间空房，英语中较早的「空、虚」义支持了用它形容眼里空无一物的样子。

senses.title: A pointless, wasted stretch of time or effort
senses.titleCN: 无所事事的状态；虚耗的光阴
senses.definition: the state of going on without purpose, interest, or useful occupation
senses.definitionCN: 没有目的、兴趣或有益活动地持续着的状态
senses.example: The long winter brought a sense of vacuity to the small town.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的冬天给这座小镇带来一种无所事事的空荡感。
senses.why: Because the noun can name emptiness in general, it also names empty stretches of life, when the hours pass with nothing filling them.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既然可泛指空，也就能指生命中空荡的时段——时间过去了，却没有任何东西填满它。

intro.en: Vacuity comes from Latin vacuitas, emptiness, from vacuus, empty, and entered English in the sixteenth century through later Latin and French forms.
intro.cn: vacuity 来自拉丁语 vacuitas（空），源于 vacuus（空的），十六世纪经由晚期拉丁语与法语形式进入英语。

items.en: The adjective vacuus describes a place or vessel with nothing in it.
items.cn: 形容词 vacuus 描述空无一物的地点或容器。

items.en: Vacuitas gives the abstract noun for emptiness or freedom from something.
items.cn: vacuitas 提供表示「空」或「免于某物」的抽象名词。

items.en: A related form vacuite, found in older French, helps carry the noun into English.
items.cn: 旧法语中与之相关的形式 vacuite 协助把这个名词带入英语。

items.en: Vacuity first names empty space, then a lack of substance in words or minds.
items.cn: vacuitas 先指空无一物的空间，随后指言辞或头脑中缺乏实质。

items.en: Modern writing uses vacuity mainly for shameless emptiness of thought and for a blank look.
items.cn: 现代写作中，vacuity 主要用于指思想的空洞和茫然的神情。

note.en: Vacuity is the noun of emptiness, close to vacuous and the vac- word family and to emptiness, inanity, and hollowness.
note.cn: vacuity 是表示「空」的名词，与 vacuous 及 vac- 词族相邻，也与 emptiness、inanity、hollowness 同属意义场。

entries.definition: empty of thought or substance
a space with no air in it
empty and available for use
the state of containing nothing
silly and pointless emptiness of content
the quality of being empty inside or insincere

normalIntro.en: Vacuity is emptiness turned serious: a phrase, a look, or a stretch of life with nothing inside.
normalIntro.cn: vacuity 是把「空」说得很严肃：一句话、一个眼神或一段生活，里面什么都没有。

normal.en: The stem vac- is Latin vacuus, empty, so the word pictures an empty vessel.
normal.cn: 词干 vac- 来自拉丁语 vacuus（空的），因此这个词描绘一只空容器。

normal.en: The ending -ity forms an abstract noun of state, as in vacuity and clarity.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ity 构成表示状态的抽象名词，如 vacuity 与 clarity。

normal.en: The adjective vacuous is far more common in daily speech than its noun.
normal.cn: 在日常口语中，形容词 vacuous 比它的名词形式常用得多。

normal.en: The verb evacuate also carries the same empty root, as in to empty out a building.
normal.cn: 动词 evacuate 也带着同一个「空」的词根，如把一栋楼清空。

normal.en: Compare emptiness: emptiness names a bare lack, while vacuity usually criticises a person or a text for being hollow.
normal.cn: 对比 emptiness：emptiness 只是指空，vacuity 通常带有批评，说人或作品空洞。

abstract.en: Hear a thin glass tapped and left ringing in an empty room.
abstract.cn: 听见一只薄玻璃杯被敲响，在空房间里嗡嗡回声。

abstract.en: See a speech bubble rising from a mouth with nothing written inside it.
abstract.cn: 看见一个气泡从嘴边冒出，里面一个字也没有。

abstract.en: Picture a face in a waiting room whose eyes are open but nobody is at home.
abstract.cn: 想象候诊室里的一个人睁着眼，可像是没人在家。

examples.en: The report was noted less for its argument than for its vacuity.
examples.cn: 这份报告引人注目的不是论点，而是它的空洞。

examples.en: She stared at the page with a vacuity that worried her teacher.
examples.cn: 她茫然地盯着那一页，这种神情让老师担忧。

examples.en: Long slogans often hide a deep vacuity of ideas.
examples.cn: 冗长的口号往往掩藏着思想的极度空洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哇，缺 it」——一句「哇，缺东西」，正好点上「空」的核心义；也可以记成「va-空 + cuity」，读起来像在敲一只空杯子；这只是谐音与拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vacuus（空的）→ 晚期拉丁语 vacuitas（空）→ 旧法语 vacuite → 英语 vacuity，核心义「空荡荡、没有实质」。

sensesIntro.en: Vacuity begins with emptiness of content in speech or art, moves to an empty look on a face, and finally covers empty, purposeless stretches of life.
sensesIntro.cn: vacuity 先指言论或作品中缺乏实质的空洞，再指脸上空洞的神情，最后涵盖没有目的、虚耗的生活时段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin empty glass on a table, ringing when it is struck.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上薄薄的空玻璃杯，一敲就嗡嗡作响。

branches.en: The main modern sense criticises words, art, or plans with nothing inside.
branches.cn: 主要现代义项批评内里空洞的言辞、作品或计划。

branches.en: An empty expression shows the same hollowness on a face.
branches.cn: 空洞的表情把同样的「空」显示在脸上。

branches.en: Empty hours with no occupation are the life-scale form of the same lack.
branches.cn: 无所事事的空耗时光，是这种匮乏在生活尺度上的形态。

branches.en: A speech that says nothing often lands on listeners as a blank stare.
branches.cn: 一无所有的讲话落到听众身上，常表现为茫然的眼神。

branches.en: Both hollow talk and empty days are time filled by nothing that matters.
branches.cn: 空洞的言辞与空荡的日子，都是被无意义之物填满的时间。

intro.en: Vacuity is built on the Latin stem vacu-, empty, which also gives vacuum, vacant, vacuous, and evacuate in English.
intro.cn: vacuity 建立在拉丁语词干 vacu-（空的）之上，同一词干在英语中还有 vacuum、vacant、vacuous 与 evacuate。

latinIntro.en: Latin vacuus means empty, and words made from it name empty spaces, empty vessels, and empty minds.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vacuus 意为空的，由它构成的词可指空的空间、空的容器和空的头脑。

items.example: Vacuus is the source of the whole vac- family.
items.exampleCN: vacuus 是整个 vac- 词族的来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity turns an adjective of state into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 把表状态的形容词变为名词。

items.example: Vacuous is the adjective that shares the root.
items.exampleCN: vacuous 是共享该词根的形容词。

items.example: He nodded vacuously during the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 会议中他空洞地点头。

items.example: A vacuum is an empty space taken literally.
items.exampleCN: vacuum 是按字面理解的空的空间。

items.example: A vacant seat is one no one has taken.
items.exampleCN: vacant 座位是没人坐的座位。

items.example: The prefix e- plus vau- makes evacuate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 e- 加表示空的词干构成 evacuate。

items.example: To evacuate a hall is to empty it of people.
items.exampleCN: evacuate 一个大厅就是把人清空。

items.example: Hollow is the everyday word for the same idea.
items.exampleCN: hollow 是同一想法的日常用词。

definition_zh: 空洞的；无意义的；茫然的；无所用心的
definition_en: showing no real thought, purpose, or interest, so that it seems empty inside
core_image: 一个张着嘴的笑脸贴纸，撕开一看背面什么都没写，风一吹就飘走
scene: 有人在电视访谈里不停重复好听的口号，被追问具体怎么做时只会笑而不答。The host called the answer vacuous and moved on.
sceneCN: 这里 vacuous 是「空洞的」（第 1 个义项：言论缺少实质、没有思想内容）；句意：主持人称这个回答空洞，于是换了话题。

pos.zh: 空洞的；无意义的；茫然无神的；无所用心的

derivatives.zh: 由 vacuous 的同源拉丁名词 vacuitas 构成，义为「空洞；空虚」
由 vacuous 加 -ly 构成，义为「空洞地；茫然地」
由 vacuous 加 -ness 构成，义为「空洞无物」
同源词，来自拉丁语 vacuus，义为「真空；空白」

senses.title: Empty of content
senses.definition: lacking any real thought or information, so that words carry nothing inside them
senses.definitionCN: 缺少真正的思想或信息，话里装不下任何东西
senses.example: The interview was full of vacuous promises.
senses.exampleCN: 这次采访里满是空洞的承诺。
senses.why: Latin vacuus means empty, and language that contains nothing worth keeping is described as an empty holder, which is the first and most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vacuus 意为空的，装不下任何值得保留之物的语言就被说成一个空的容器，这是最常见的第一义项。

senses.title: A blank face or gaze
senses.definition: having an expression that shows no thought, feeling, or awareness
senses.definitionCN: 表情上不显示思考、情感或觉察的样子
senses.example: He gave a vacuous smile and changed the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 他笑了笑，神情空洞，随即换了话题。
senses.why: The same image of an empty vessel extends from words to faces, so a person who seems absent behind the eyes is called vacuous.
senses.whyCN: 空容器的意象从言语延伸到面孔，眼里像没人在场的人就被称为 vacuous。

senses.title: Lazy, unthinking habits
senses.titleCN: 无所用心的；懒得思考的
senses.definition: describing a way of living or working that goes on without curiosity or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 形容一种没有好奇心、没有目的的生活方式或工作方式
senses.example: Critics complained about a vacuous culture of pure shopping.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抱怨一种只有购物的浅薄文化。
senses.why: Once the adjective means without substance, it easily criticises habits and lifestyles that fill their time without thinking, an extension rather than a separate root.
senses.whyCN: 形容词一旦表示「无实质」，就很容易用来批评那些不思考、只是把时间填满的生活习惯，这属于延伸而非另一个词根。

intro.en: Vacuous comes from Latin vacuus, empty, and reached English through Latin as an adjective for things or people with nothing inside.
intro.cn: vacuous 来自拉丁语 vacuus（空的），作为形容内里空空之物或人的形容词经拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Vacuus means empty, void, or free from something.
items.cn: vacuus 意为空的、虚的、免于某物的。

items.en: English adopts vacuous, at first for empty space and idle leisure.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪采用 vacuous，最初用于空无一物的空间和闲散无事。

items.en: Writers begin to apply the adjective to words and thoughts without substance.
items.cn: 作家开始把这个形容词用于没有实质的言辞和思想。

items.en: The word extends to faces and to people seen as having nothing in their minds.
items.cn: 该词延伸到面部表情，也用于被看作头脑空空的人。

items.en: Modern speech uses vacuous mostly as a criticism of empty talk or a blank look.
items.cn: 现代用语中，vacuous 多用来批评空洞的言论或茫然的表情。

note.en: Vacuous is the adjective of emptiness, close to vacuity and the vac- family and to empty, hollow, and inane.
note.cn: vacuous 是表示「空」的形容词，与 vacuity 及 vac- 词族相邻，也与 empty、hollow、inane 同属意义场。

entries.definition: empty lack of thought or content
a space with no air
empty and unoccupied
containing nothing at all
empty inside or lacking real feeling
silly and without meaning
entries.definitionCN: 愚蠢空洞的；毫无意义的

normalIntro.en: Vacuous keeps the Latin picture of an empty vessel and applies it to words, looks, and habits.
normalIntro.cn: vacuous 保留了拉丁语空容器的画面，并把它用到言语、神情和习惯上。

normal.en: The stem vacu- is Latin vacuus, empty, so the adjective literally means empty of thought.
normal.cn: 词干 vacu- 来自拉丁语 vacuus（空的），因此这个形容词字面上就是「思想空」。

normal.en: The suffix -ous means full of or having, so vacuous reads as having emptiness.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ous 意为「充满……的、具有……的」，所以 vacuous 读作「带有空」。

normal.en: The noun vacuity and the adverb vacuously are built from the same adjective.
normal.cn: 名词 vacuity 与副词 vacuously 都由这个形容词构成。

normal.en: The same root appears in vacancy, which names an empty room rather than an empty remark.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 vacancy 中，它指空着的座位或病房，而不是空话。

normal.en: Compare hollow: hollow can describe a physical shape, while vacuous is mostly a judgement on talk or people.
normal.cn: 对比 hollow：hollow 可描述物理形态，vacuous 更多是对言论或人的评价。

abstract.en: See a speech bubble that looks bright but rustles when you hold it up to the light.
abstract.cn: 看见一个气泡看起来鲜亮，举到光下却哗啦作响、里面空空。

abstract.en: Picture a smile painted on a paper mask, with no face behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象纸面具上画着笑容，后面却没有脸。

abstract.en: Think of a shopping trolley rolling on with a dozen bright packets and nothing to cook.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆购物车推着十来袋鲜艳零食，却没有一样能做菜。

examples.en: She grew tired of vacuous small talk at the party.
examples.cn: 她对聚会上空洞的闲聊感到厌倦。

examples.en: The film looks beautiful but its story feels vacuous.
examples.cn: 这部电影画面很美，故事却显得空洞。

examples.en: He responded vacuously and then walked away.
examples.cn: 他茫然地应了一声，然后走开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哇，缺」——一句「哇，缺！」正好是词干 vacu（空）再加感叹；可以记成「空得只剩一声哇」；这只是谐音与拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vacuus（空的）→ 拉丁语 vacuitas（空）→ 英语 vacuous，核心义「里面什么都没有」。

sensesIntro.en: Vacuous starts as a judgement on words that carry nothing, extends to faces that show no thought, and then to whole habits of life without curiosity or purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: vacuous 先用来评判装不下任何东西的言辞，再扩展到没有思想的脸色，最后延伸到整段缺乏好奇与目的的生活方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright mask with nothing behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张鲜亮的面具，后面空无一物。

branches.en: The commonest modern sense criticises speech that carries no thought.
branches.cn: 最常见的现代义项批评不带思想的言语。

branches.en: A face with no one behind it gives the sense of blankness.
branches.cn: 后面没人的面孔给出了「茫然」这一义项。

branches.en: Empty habits turn the adjective into criticism of a whole way of life.
branches.cn: 空虚的习惯把这个形容词变成对一整套生活方式的批评。

branches.en: Hollow talk and a blank stare are two surfaces of the same emptiness.
branches.cn: 空洞的话语与茫然的眼神是同一片空虚的两个表面。

branches.en: Words without content and lives without purpose are graded forms of the same lack.
branches.cn: 没有内容的言辞与没有目的的生活，是同一匮乏的不同程度形态。

intro.en: Vacuous is built on Latin vacuus, empty, with the familiar Latin ending -ous, and it belongs with vacuum, vacant, vacuity, and evacuate.
intro.cn: vacuous 由拉丁语 vacuus（空的）加上熟悉的拉丁词尾 -ous 构成，与 vacuum、vacant、vacuity、evacuate 同属一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vacuus means empty, and an ending like -ous makes an adjective meaning having the quality of.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vacuus 意为空的，类似 -ous 的词尾构成表示「具有某种性质」的形容词。

items.example: Vacuus is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: vacuus 是整个词族的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ous makes a quality adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成性质形容词。

items.meaning: in a blank or hollow manner
items.example: He smiled vacuously at the camera.
items.exampleCN: 他对着镜头空洞地微笑。

items.example: Vacuity is the noun of the same idea.
items.exampleCN: vacuity 是同一想法的名词形式。

items.example: A vacant post is one nobody fills.
items.exampleCN: vacant post 是无人担任的职位。

items.example: The prefix e- gives evacuate its draining sense.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 e- 让 evacuate 带有排出、清空之意。

items.example: To evacuate a building is to empty it.
items.exampleCN: evacuate 一座楼就是把它清空。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms vacuousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 vacuousness。

items.example: Hollow is the everyday word for empty inside.
items.exampleCN: hollow 是「内里空」的日常用词。

definition_zh: 英勇；勇气；勇猛；豪勇
definition_en: great courage, especially in the face of danger or in battle
core_image: 战场上挺直脊背向前的一步，明知危险仍然迈出
scene: 老兵胸前别着奖章，那是表彰他在危急关头的英勇。The old soldier wore a medal for his valor in the battle.
sceneCN: 这里 valor 是「英勇」（第 1 个义项：临危不惧的勇气）；句意：这位老兵佩戴着因战斗中的英勇而获颁的奖章。

pos.zh: 英勇；勇气；勇猛

derivatives.zh: 由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「英勇的」
同一拉丁词根借古法语而来，义为「勇敢的；英勇的」
英式拼写变体，义也为「英勇」
由 valorous 加副词后缀构成，义为「英勇地」

senses.title: Courage in battle
senses.definition: bold courage shown in fighting or in great danger
senses.definitionCN: 在战斗或巨大危险中表现出的无畏勇气
senses.example: The regiment was praised for its valor.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团因英勇而受到表彰。
senses.why: The Latin root valere means to be strong and worthy, so valor names the strength of spirit that stands firm in battle.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 valere 意为「强健、有价值」，所以 valor 指在战斗中屹立不动的精神力量。

senses.title: Personal bravery
senses.definition: the quality of being personally brave when facing difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 面对困难时个人所具备的勇敢品质
senses.example: She showed real valor in defending her friend.
senses.exampleCN: 她为保护朋友表现出真正的勇气。
senses.why: As the word moved into everyday English, the battlefield frame loosened, and valor became any personal courage.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词进入日常英语后，战场的框架被放宽，valor 泛指任何个人的勇气。

senses.title: Heroic deed
senses.definition: a brave act that deserves praise
senses.definitionCN: 值得称赞的勇敢行为
senses.example: His valor that night saved three children.
senses.exampleCN: 他那晚的英勇行为救了三个孩子。
senses.why: Because courage is counted by the deeds it produces, the word also names the brave act itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为勇气要靠它所产生的行动来衡量，这个词也用来指勇敢的行为本身。

intro.en: Valor goes back to Latin valere, to be strong or to be worth, through Old French valour.
intro.cn: valor 上溯拉丁语 valere（强健、有价值），经古法语 valour 进入英语。

items.en: Valere means to be strong or to be worth something.
items.cn: valere 意为强健或有价值。

items.en: Valor means worth, value, or courage.
items.cn: valor 意为价值、可贵或勇气。

items.en: Valour carries both worth and courage into French.
items.cn: valour 把「价值」与「勇气」双重含义带入法语。

items.en: The word enters English meaning worth and brave courage.
items.cn: 该词在十四世纪进入英语，兼指价值与英勇。

items.en: Modern English keeps valor mainly for battle courage, with valour as the British spelling.
items.cn: 现代英语中 valor 主要保留「战场勇气」义，英式拼写为 valour。

note.en: Valor sits in the valere family, which also gathers value, valid, and valiant.
note.cn: valor 属于 valere 词族，同一词族还有 value、valid 与 valiant。

entries.definition: very brave
showing valor
worth or usefulness
the quality of being brave
the ability to do something dangerous without fear
very great bravery in a good cause

normalIntro.en: Valor is courage drawn from the Latin idea of strength and worth.
normalIntro.cn: valor 是从拉丁语「强健、有价值」这一观念中抽出的勇气。

normal.en: Show valor is a fixed pairing in formal writing.
normal.cn: show valor 是正式写作中的固定搭配。

normal.en: Valiant and valor share the valere root.
normal.cn: valiant 与 valor 共享 valere 词根。

normal.en: Value and valor both mean worth in Latin.
normal.cn: value 与 valor 在拉丁语中都表示「价值」。

normal.en: A medal for valor honors a brave deed.
normal.cn: a medal for valor 表彰英勇行为。

normal.en: British writers spell the word valour.
normal.cn: 英式英语把该词拼作 valour。

abstract.en: Picture a soldier stepping forward when others step back.
abstract.cn: 想象别人后退时，一名士兵向前迈出一步。

abstract.en: Think of someone shielding a stranger from danger.
abstract.cn: 想象有人为陌生人挡住危险。

abstract.en: See a hand pulling a child out of the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把孩子从水中拉出来。

examples.en: The young officer was decorated for valor.
examples.cn: 这位年轻军官因英勇获得勋章。

examples.en: Her valor in the emergency impressed everyone present.
examples.cn: 她在紧急情况下的勇气让在场所有人都很敬佩。

examples.en: Ancient poems often celebrate the valor of fallen soldiers.
examples.cn: 古诗常常歌颂阵亡将士的英勇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哇，老虎」——面对老虎还敢向前，便是英勇；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 valere（强健、有价值）→ 拉丁语 valor（价值；勇气）→ 古法语 valour → 英语 valor／valour，核心义「值得称许的力量」。

sensesIntro.en: Valor starts with courage on the battlefield, widens to personal bravery, and finally names the brave deed itself.
sensesIntro.cn: valor 从战场上的勇气出发，扩展到个人的勇敢品质，最后指英勇行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step forward while others step back.
core.cn: 核心意象：别人后退时向前迈出的一步。

branches.en: Battle courage is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 战场勇气是最古老的义项。

branches.en: Personal bravery is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 个人勇气是日常义项。

branches.en: A heroic deed is the concrete outcome of courage.
branches.cn: 英勇行为是勇气产生的具体结果。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of standing firm under threat.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「在威胁面前屹立不动」的观念。

branches.en: The quality of valor is proved by the deed of valor.
branches.cn: 英勇的品质要靠英勇的行为来证明。

intro.en: Valor is a Latin noun of worth and courage, with valiant, valorous, and value in its family.
intro.cn: valor 是拉丁语中表示「价值与勇气」的名词，其词族包括 valiant、valorous 与 value。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere means to be strong, and valor means worth or courage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere 意为强健，valor 意为价值或勇气。

items.meaning: to be strong, to be worth
items.example: Valere gives the strength image.
items.exampleCN: valere 提供「强健」的意象。

items.example: Valor is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: valor 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms valorous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 valorous。

items.example: Valorous describes a brave person.
items.exampleCN: valorous 描述英勇的人。

items.example: Valiant comes from the same root.
items.exampleCN: valiant 来自同一词根。

items.example: Value keeps the worth sense.
items.exampleCN: value 保留「价值」含义。

items.example: Valid also comes from valere.
items.exampleCN: valid 也来自 valere。

items.example: Valour is the British spelling.
items.exampleCN: valour 是英式拼写。

definition_zh: 清漆；罩光漆；上清漆；涂饰；粉饰
definition_en: a clear liquid that dries into a hard shiny coat, or to coat something with it
core_image: 刷子在木板上走一遍，木头立刻泛起一层亮膜
scene: 木匠把最后一层清漆涂在刚做好的桌面上。The carpenter put a final coat of varnish on the new table.
sceneCN: 这里 varnish 是「清漆」（第 1 个义项：涂成光亮硬膜的透明液体）；句意：木匠在刚做好的桌子上刷了最后一道清漆。

pos.zh: 清漆；罩光漆
给……上清漆；粉饰；掩饰

derivatives.zh: 由动词过去分词转成形容词，义为「上过清漆的」
由现在分词转成的名词，义为「上漆的过程」
加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「上漆的人」
加否定前缀 -un 构成，义为「未上漆的；不加掩饰的」

senses.title: A clear glossy coating
senses.definition: a transparent liquid that dries into a hard shiny film on wood or other surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 涂在木头等表面后干结成光亮硬膜的透明液体
senses.example: The varnish on the floor is wearing thin.
senses.exampleCN: 地板上的清漆越磨越薄了。
senses.why: The word is usually traced to medieval Greek berenike, a resin brought from the region of the same name, so the substance is named after where it came from.
senses.whyCN: 一般认为该词源自中世纪希腊语 berenike，即从同名地区运来的树脂，所以这种物质是以产地命名的。

senses.title: To coat with varnish
senses.definition: to put varnish on a surface so that it looks smooth and stays protected
senses.definitionCN: 在表面上涂清漆，使其看起来光滑并受到保护
senses.example: They varnished the wooden floor before moving in.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搬进来之前给木地板上了清漆。
senses.why: Once the substance had a name, the action of applying it simply took the same word as a verb.
senses.whyCN: 这种物质有了名称之后，涂上它的动作就直接借用同一个词作动词。

senses.title: To give a false shine to
senses.definition: to make something bad or plain look better than it really is
senses.definitionCN: 把不好的或平淡的事物说得比实际更好
senses.example: The report varnishes over the company losses.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告粉饰了公司的亏损。
senses.why: Because varnish adds shine without changing what lies beneath, the word became a metaphor for glossing over faults.
senses.whyCN: 因为清漆只是添加光泽，并不改变下面的东西，于是这个词成了掩饰缺点的比喻。

senses.title: Nail polish
senses.definition: a cosmetic liquid painted on the nails and dried to a glossy film
senses.definitionCN: 涂在指甲上、干燥后形成光膜的化妆液
senses.example: She wore pale pink varnish on her nails.
senses.exampleCN: 她指甲上涂着浅粉色的指甲油。
senses.why: In British English the glossy coating extends from wood to fingernails, where the effect is the same.
senses.whyCN: 在英式英语中，这种光亮涂层从木头延伸到指甲，因为效果是一样的。

senses.title: A layer over the outside
senses.definition: a thin layer that hides the real substance of something
senses.definitionCN: 遮盖事物真实本质的薄薄一层
senses.example: Their politeness was only a thin varnish.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的礼貌只是一层薄薄的虚饰。
senses.why: Any thin coating that hides what is beneath can be called a varnish, so the word names a false surface generally.
senses.whyCN: 任何遮盖下方事物的薄薄涂层都可称作 varnish，因此该词泛指虚假的表面。

intro.en: Varnish is usually traced through Old French vernis to medieval Latin veronice, from Greek berenike, a resin from the city of Berenice.
intro.cn: varnish 一般认为经古法语 vernis 上溯中世纪拉丁语 veronice，再追溯到希腊语 berenike，即产自贝勒尼基城的树脂。

items.en: Berenike is a city and the name of the resin traded there.
items.cn: berenike 是一座城市的名字，也指当地交易的树脂。

items.en: Veronice names the resin and glossy liquid in Latin use.
items.cn: 在拉丁语用法中 veronice 指这种树脂与光亮液体。

items.en: Vernis names a glossy coating used on wood.
items.cn: vernis 指用于木材的光亮涂层。

items.en: Vernisshe appears in English with the same painting sense.
items.cn: vernisshe 以相同的涂饰含义出现在英语中。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative sense of glossing over faults and the noun nail varnish.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「粉饰缺点」的比喻义与「指甲油」这一名词用法。

note.en: Varnish belongs with coatings and polishes, and also with verbs of hiding the truth.
note.cn: varnish 与各类涂层、抛光剂同属一类，也与掩盖真相的动词同属一类。

entries.definition: covered with varnish
not varnished, or plainly stated
to lose shine or to spoil a reputation
entries.definitionCN: 失去光泽；损害名誉，只是拼写相似，词源不同

entries.definition: a hard shiny coating made from resin
a substance rubbed on to make something shine
a smooth shiny surface

normalIntro.en: Varnish names the coat, the act of painting it, and the shine that hides what is underneath.
normalIntro.cn: varnish 既指那层漆，也指刷漆的动作，还指掩盖底下事物的光泽。

normal.en: A coat of varnish is a layer of glossy paint.
normal.cn: a coat of varnish 就是一层亮漆。

normal.en: To varnish a table means to paint it with varnish.
normal.cn: varnish a table 就是给桌子上清漆。

normal.en: Varnish the truth means to hide its rough parts with a shine.
normal.cn: varnish the truth 就是用光亮把真相粗糙的部分遮住。

normal.en: The British use nail varnish where Americans say nail polish.
normal.cn: 英式说 nail varnish，美式则说 nail polish。

normal.en: Unvarnished news is news told without a glossy finish.
normal.cn: unvarnished news 指没有经过粉饰的新闻。

abstract.en: Picture a brush leaving a wet shining line on dark wood.
abstract.cn: 想象刷子在深色木头上留下一道湿润发亮的痕迹。

abstract.en: See a worn table turn glossy under the brush.
abstract.cn: 想象一张旧桌子在刷子下重新变得光亮。

abstract.en: Think of a thin coat that makes a rough board look neat.
abstract.cn: 想象薄薄一层漆让粗糙的木板看起来整齐。

examples.en: The old chest still has its original varnish.
examples.cn: 这只旧箱子还保留着原来的清漆。

examples.en: They varnished the boat before the race.
examples.cn: 比赛前他们给船上了清漆。

examples.en: His polite words could not varnish the truth.
examples.cn: 他客气的话语也无法掩饰真相。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瓦尼诗」——木头刷上漆，亮得像一首诗；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源自中世纪希腊语 berenike（小亚细亚贝勒尼基城所产树脂）→ 中世纪拉丁语 veronice → 古法语 vernis → 英语 varnish，核心义「光亮涂层」。

sensesIntro.en: Varnish starts as the glossy coating itself, moves to the act of applying it, and then to the cosmetic shine and the false shine of covered faults.
sensesIntro.cn: varnish 先指光亮涂层本身，再指涂刷的动作，然后扩展到美甲的亮油与掩盖缺点的虚假光泽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brush leaving a glossy film on wood.
core.cn: 核心意象：刷子在木头上留下的一层亮膜。

branches.en: The coating itself is the core noun sense.
branches.cn: 涂层本身是核心名词义项。

branches.en: Applying the coating is the verb sense.
branches.cn: 涂上涂层是动词义项。

branches.en: Glossing over faults is the figurative verb sense.
branches.cn: 掩盖缺点是比喻性的动词义项。

branches.en: Nail varnish uses the shiny surface for a cosmetic.
branches.cn: 指甲油把光亮表面用于美容。

branches.en: Both the metaphor and the thin layer name a false outside.
branches.cn: 比喻用法与薄层用法都指虚假的外表。

intro.en: Varnish is a loan word from French, and its family is built with the endings -ed, -ing, -er, and the prefix un-.
intro.cn: varnish 是从法语借来的词，它的词族靠 -ed、-ing、-er 词尾与 un- 前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The medieval Latin form veronice is the link between Greek berenike and Old French vernis.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语形式 veronice 是希腊语 berenike 与古法语 vernis 之间的桥梁。

items.example: Vernis is the direct French source.
items.exampleCN: vernis 是直接的法语来源。

items.example: Veronice is the Latin bridge form.
items.exampleCN: veronice 是拉丁语中的过渡形式。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms varnished.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 varnished。

items.example: Varnished describes a coated surface.
items.exampleCN: varnished 描述上过漆的表面。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms varnishing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 varnishing。

items.example: The suffix -er forms varnisher.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 varnisher。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unvarnished.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unvarnished。

items.example: Unvarnished means plain and honest.
items.exampleCN: unvarnished 表示朴实无华的。

definition_zh: 极大地；非常；巨大地；广泛地
definition_en: to a very great degree or extent
core_image: 站在平原中央望向地平线，四周什么都装不下，只剩辽阔
scene: 两座城市的规模相差极大，从高空一眼就能看出。Seen from high above, the scale of the two cities differs vastly.
sceneCN: 这里 vastly 是「极大地」（第 1 个义项：程度非常之大）；句意：从高空望去，两座城市的规模相差极大。

pos.zh: 极大地；非常；广泛地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -ly 得到的基础形容词，义为「巨大的；辽阔的」
加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「辽阔；巨大」
罕见名词形式，义为「广阔；浩大」

senses.title: To a very great degree
senses.definition: to an extremely large degree
senses.definitionCN: 达到非常大的程度
senses.example: The two proposals are vastly different.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个提案差别很大。
senses.why: Vast comes from Latin vastus, meaning empty and wide, so vastly says that a gap or degree is as wide as open space.
senses.whyCN: vast 源自拉丁语 vastus，意为空旷辽阔，所以 vastly 表示差距或程度像空旷之地一样大。

senses.title: Much more than
senses.definition: by a very large amount when compared with someone or something else
senses.definitionCN: 与他人或他物相比，在数量上超出一大截
senses.example: The new engine is vastly more efficient.
senses.exampleCN: 新引擎的效率要高得多。
senses.why: The adverb usually attaches to comparatives, so the wide space becomes a measurable gap between two things.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词常跟在比较级后面，于是辽阔的空间就变成了两件事之间可测量的差距。

senses.title: Over a wide extent
senses.definition: on a large scale or over a wide area
senses.definitionCN: 以大尺度或在宽广范围之内
senses.example: Prices vary vastly from city to city.
senses.exampleCN: 各城市之间的价格差别很大。
senses.why: Because vast can describe how far something spreads, vastly also names changes that cover a wide extent.
senses.whyCN: 因为 vast 可以描述事物扩展多广，所以 vastly 也用来指覆盖范围很广的变化。

intro.en: Vastly is vast plus the adverb ending -ly; vast comes from Latin vastus, empty and wide.
intro.cn: vastly 由 vast 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；vast 源自拉丁语 vastus，意为空旷辽阔。

items.en: Vastus means empty, desolate, or widely spread.
items.cn: vastus 意为空旷、荒凉或散布极广。

items.en: Vaste appears in French with the sense of huge and wide.
items.cn: vaste 在法语中出现，意为巨大辽阔。

items.en: Vast enters English as an adjective for great size.
items.cn: vast 作为表示巨大尺寸的形容词进入英语。

items.en: The adverb vastly is formed with -ly and first means in a wide manner.
items.cn: 副词 vastly 由 -ly 构成，起初意为辽阔地、广泛地。

items.en: Modern English uses vastly mostly for a very large difference in degree.
items.cn: 现代英语中 vastly 主要用于程度上的巨大差别。

note.en: Vastly is the adverb of vast, a word for empty space, and it often partners comparatives.
note.cn: vastly 是 vast 的副词形式，vast 本指空旷的空间，而它常与比较级连用。

entries.definition: extremely large in area or amount
the quality of being vast
the most vast
to a large degree
very much
by a noticeable amount

normalIntro.en: Vastly borrows its size from vast, so it always says that a gap is wide.
normalIntro.cn: vastly 的「大小」来自 vast，所以它总在说差距很大。

normal.en: Vastly different describes things far apart from each other.
normal.cn: vastly different 形容两者相差很远。

normal.en: Vastly superior means much better than the other.
normal.cn: vastly superior 意为优越得多。

normal.en: The -ly ending turns the adjective vast into an adverb.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 把形容词 vast 变成副词。

normal.en: Vastness is the noun for the open width of something.
normal.cn: vastness 是表示「辽阔」的名词。

normal.en: Keep vastly for huge gaps, not for small differences.
normal.cn: vastly 用于巨大的差距，别用来形容小差别。

abstract.en: Picture two lines whose gaps keep widening.
abstract.cn: 想象两条线之间的缝隙不断变宽。

abstract.en: See a small engine and a huge one side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象一台小引擎和一台巨大的引擎并排放着。

abstract.en: Think of one dot in the middle of a blank map.
abstract.cn: 想象空白地图中央的一个小点。

examples.en: Living costs are vastly higher in the capital.
examples.cn: 首都的生活成本要高得多。

examples.en: The new method is vastly more reliable.
examples.cn: 新方法要可靠得多。

examples.en: Their opinions on the plan were vastly different.
examples.cn: 他们对这个计划的看法差别很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挖死他」——挖开一整片，地大得看不到边，便是巨大；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vastus（空旷的、荒凉的）→ 古法语 vaste → 英语 vast（辽阔的）→ vast + -ly = vastly，核心义「空间辽阔」转指「程度巨大」。

sensesIntro.en: Vastly first marks a very great degree, then a wide gap in comparisons, and finally a wide extent.
sensesIntro.cn: vastly 先表示程度极大，再表示比较中的巨大差距，最后表示宽广的范围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open plain that stretches to the horizon.
core.cn: 核心意象：一直延伸到地平线的空旷平原。

branches.en: A great degree is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 程度极大是日常义项。

branches.en: A wide gap appears when vastly meets a comparative.
branches.cn: 当 vastly 与比较级相遇，就出现巨大差距。

branches.en: A wide extent keeps the original spatial image.
branches.cn: 宽广范围保留了原本的空间意象。

branches.en: Both senses say that the distance between two things is large.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在说两件事之间的距离很大。

branches.en: A wide spread of change is the same width measured over an area.
branches.cn: 广泛的变化就是在面上量出的同一份宽度。

intro.en: Vastly is built from the Latin stem vast plus the English adverb ending -ly, and lives with vast and vastness.
intro.cn: vastly 由拉丁词干 vast 加英语副词词尾 -ly 构成，与 vast、vastness 同属一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vastus means empty and wide, and it passes into English through Old French vaste.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vastus 意为空旷辽阔，经古法语 vaste 传入英语。

items.example: Vastus gives the empty plain image.
items.exampleCN: vastus 提供空旷平原的意象。

items.example: Vast is the base adjective.
items.exampleCN: vast 是基础形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms vastly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 vastly。

items.example: Vastly marks a great degree.
items.exampleCN: vastly 表示程度极大。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms vastness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 vastness。

items.example: Vastness names the open width.
items.exampleCN: vastness 指辽阔的宽度。

items.example: The suffix -est forms vastest.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -est 构成 vastest。

items.example: Vastest is the superlative form.
items.exampleCN: vastest 是最高级形式。

definition_zh: 向量；矢量；传播媒介；航线
definition_en: a quantity with both size and direction, such as a force, or the carrier that transmits a disease or piece of code
core_image: 一支带箭头的短箭头，从原点伸出，指向某个方向
scene: 数学老师在黑板上画出一个带箭头的线段，说明力是有方向的量。The maths teacher drew an arrow on the board to show that force is a vector.
sceneCN: 这里 vector 是「向量、矢量」（第 1 个义项：既有大小又有方向的量）；句意：数学老师在黑板上画出一个箭头，说明力是一个矢量。

pos.zh: 向量；矢量；媒介；航线

collocations.zh: 疾病媒介；传播疾病的生物
攻击途径；漏洞利用入口

derivatives.zh: 向量加 -ial 构成，义为「矢量的；带方向的」
向量加 -ize 构成，义为「向量化；按向量方式处理」
vectorize 加 -ation 构成（英式拼写），义为「向量化」

senses.title: A quantity with size and direction
senses.definition: a quantity, such as force or velocity, that has both size and direction
senses.definitionCN: 具有大小和方向的量，如力或速度
senses.example: Force and velocity are both vectors in physics.
senses.exampleCN: 在物理学中，力和速度都是矢量。
senses.why: The Latin word named the one who carries, and a vector carries you along a definite direction with a definite strength.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词原指「运送者」，而矢量正是带着确定方向、确定大小的量，像一名把东西送往某处的搬运者。

senses.title: A group of numbers in algebra
senses.definition: an ordered list of numbers treated as a single object in mathematics
senses.definitionCN: 数学中作为一个整体处理的一组有序数字
senses.example: Add the two vectors by adding each of their components.
senses.exampleCN: 把两个向量的对应分量分别相加。
senses.why: Pure mathematics kept the direction idea as a list of components, each one a distance along an axis.
senses.whyCN: 纯数学保留了「方向」的想法，只是换成分量列表：每个分量就是沿一根轴的位移，方向感藏在分量之中。

senses.title: An animal or organism that transmits disease
senses.definition: a living creature that carries a disease from one person or animal to another
senses.definitionCN: 把疾病从一个人或动物传给另一个的活体生物
senses.example: Mosquitoes are the main vector for malaria.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子是疟疾的主要传播媒介。
senses.why: The carrier image returns literally: the insect carries the germ along a fixed route.
senses.whyCN: 「运送者」的画面在这里回到字面：蚊虫像一条固定的运输线，把病菌从一处送到另一处。

senses.title: A direction of travel in aviation
senses.definition: a direction given for a pilot or air traffic controller to fly in
senses.definitionCN: 给飞行员或空管员指定的飞行方向
senses.example: The controller cleared the jet to turn to a new vector.
senses.exampleCN: 空管员准许这架喷气机转向新的航向。
senses.why: In the air a vector is literally an arrow: control tells the plane which way to travel from now on.
senses.whyCN: 在空中，vector 就是一个字面上的箭头：空管告诉飞机从现在起朝哪个方向飞。

senses.title: The way a piece of code spreads
senses.definition: a method or route by which a virus or an attack reaches a system
senses.definitionCN: 病毒或攻击到达系统的某种方法或路径
senses.example: Email attachments are a common attack vector.
senses.exampleCN: 电子邮件附件是常见的攻击途径。
senses.why: The biological carrier becomes digital: a file carries the code and the path is its vector.
senses.whyCN: 生物界的「携带者」被搬到数字世界：文件携带恶意代码，它进入系统的路径就是 vector。

intro.en: Vector comes from Latin vector, a carrier or one who carries, from vehere, to carry. The word was first used for mathematics in nineteenth century English.
intro.cn: vector 来自拉丁语 vector（运送者、携带者），源于动词 vehere（运送）。它在十九世纪英语中先用于数学语境。

items.en: Vehere means to carry or transport.
items.cn: vehere 意为运送、搬运。

items.en: Vector names a person or thing that carries something.
items.cn: vector 指承载某物的人或物。

items.en: Nineteenth century geometry uses vector for a line with a given direction.
items.cn: 十九世纪的几何学用 vector 指带有给定方向的有向线段。

items.en: Medicine adopts the word for a creature that carries a disease.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，医学用这个词指携带疾病的生物。

items.en: Computing and aviation extend the carrier image to code and flight paths.
items.cn: 现代英语把「携带」的意象扩展到计算机代码与飞行航线。

note.en: Vector belongs to the Latin carry family around vehere, and it sits beside the maths words magnitude and scalar.
note.cn: vector 属于围绕 vehere 的拉丁语「运送」词族，在数学用语中又与 magnitude、scalar 相邻。

entries.definition: great force or intensity
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈；强烈（与 vector 同源，都来自拉丁语 vehere）

entries.definition: a machine that carries people or goods
entries.definitionCN: 车辆；载具（同源于拉丁语「运送」）

entries.definition: relating to vectors
the size of a quantity, without direction
entries.definitionCN: 大小；量值（与矢量相对，不含方向）

entries.definition: a quantity with size but no direction
entries.definitionCN: 标量；只有大小没有方向的量

entries.definition: a person or thing that transmits a disease or message

normalIntro.en: Vector keeps the Latin image of a carrier: someone who takes something in a set direction at a set strength.
normalIntro.cn: vector 保留着拉丁语「运送者」的画面：一个按确定方向和确定力度把东西带往某处的人。

normal.en: The Latin verb vehere, to carry, also gives vehicle and vehemence.
normal.cn: 拉丁语动词 vehere（运送）同时还派生出了「vehicle」和「vehemence」。

normal.en: A vector quantity has both size and direction, unlike a scalar such as temperature.
normal.cn: 矢量既有大小又有方向，而温度这类标量没有方向。

normal.en: A mosquito acting as a vector carries a germ from one host to the next.
normal.cn: 蚊子作为「vector」（病媒），把病菌从一个宿主带到下一个。

normal.en: In computing, an attack vector is simply the route by which the code arrives.
normal.cn: 在计算机领域，「attack vector」就是恶意代码到达系统的那条路径。

normal.en: Compare vehicle: a vehicle carries people, a vector carries direction, germs, or code.
normal.cn: 对比「vehicle」：车辆运送人，vector 则运送方向、病菌或代码。

abstract.en: Picture a short arrow drawn from a dot: the length is size, the tip shows direction.
abstract.cn: 想象从一个圆点伸出的一个短箭头：长度是大小，箭尖指明方向。

abstract.en: Think of wind as an arrow in the sky showing both its strength and where it blows.
abstract.cn: 把风想象成天上一支箭头：既显示风力，也显示它吹去的方向。

abstract.en: See a mosquito landing on a sleeping traveller, carrying a fever with it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蚊子落在熟睡的旅行者身上，翅膀上带着一场热病。

examples.en: Drag is a vector that always opposes the direction of motion.
examples.cn: 阻力是一个矢量，其方向始终与运动方向相反。

examples.en: The health team studied how the vector moved between villages in the rainy season.
examples.cn: 健康调查小组研究了雨季里这种病媒如何在村庄之间移动。

examples.en: Each vector in the table lists wind speed and direction for one hour.
examples.cn: 表中每一个向量都记录了一小时内的风速与风向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克托」——一位精准的投递员，每次送货都按固定方向和力度出发；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vehere（运送）→ vector（运送者）→ 英语 vector，核心义「携带者、按方向运送者」；同族词有 vehicle。

sensesIntro.en: Vector moves from the carrier to a directed quantity, then to a list of numbers, a disease carrier, an aviation heading, and a digital route.
sensesIntro.cn: vector 从「运送者」出发，先成为有方向的量，再成为一组数字、疾病的携带者、飞行的航向，最后成为数字世界的入侵路径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow that shows length and direction at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个箭头，同时标出长度与方向。

branches.en: The directed arrow becomes a quantity with size and direction.
branches.cn: 有向箭头成为既有大小又有方向的量。

branches.en: The same idea is written as an ordered list of numbers.
branches.cn: 同一个想法被写成一组有序数字。

branches.en: The carrier picture returns for insects that pass on disease.
branches.cn: 「携带者」的画面在传播疾病的蚊虫身上回归。

branches.en: Both flying a set heading and routing code use a path of travel.
branches.cn: 指定航向与代码路径都借用「行进路线」的概念。

branches.en: The maths vector and the disease vector both carry something in one direction.
branches.cn: 数学里的矢量与疾病的病媒都是沿某一方向携带某物。

intro.en: Vector comes from the Latin root veh-, to carry, with the agent suffix -tor, so the word literally means the carrier.
intro.cn: vector 由拉丁语词根 veh-（运送）加施动后缀 -tor 构成，字面意思就是「运送者」。

latinIntro.en: Latin vehere means to carry, and vehi means to be carried; vector is the one who carries.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vehere 意为运送，vehi 意为被运送，vector 指运送的人或物。

items.example: The root veh- appears in vector and vehicle.
items.exampleCN: 词根 veh- 出现在 vector 与 vehicle 之中。

items.example: The suffix -tor marks the one who carries.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tor 标出「执行运送的人」。

items.example: Vector stands for a directed quantity.
items.exampleCN: vector 表示有方向的量。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms vectorial.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ial 构成 vectorial。

items.example: Vectorial sums follow the arrow rules.
items.exampleCN: 矢量求和遵循箭头相加的规则。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms vectorize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 vectorize。

items.meaning: to express or process as a vector
items.meaningCN: 向量化；用向量方式处理
items.example: Programmers vectorize loops for speed.
items.exampleCN: 程序员把循环向量化以提升速度。

items.example: Vehicle shares the carrying root.
items.exampleCN: vehicle 共享「运送」词根。

items.example: Vehemence also grows from the same root.
items.exampleCN: vehemence 也来自同一个词根。

definition_zh: 转向；突然改变方向；改变立场；风向变顺
definition_en: to change direction suddenly, to shift from a course or position, or of the wind to turn clockwise
core_image: 一条原本笔直的路，忽然向旁边弯了过去
scene: 高速公路前方突然出现施工标志，司机赶紧把方向盘往旁边打。A road sign warned of roadworks, so the driver had to veer to the left.
sceneCN: 这里 veer 是「突然转向」（第 1 个义项：行进中忽然改变方向）；句意：路牌提示前方施工，所以司机只好把车向左转。

pos.zh: 转向；突然改变方向；改变立场

derivatives.zh: 现在分词转成的名词，义为「改变方向；摇摆」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不转向的；坚定不移的」
现在分词转成的形容词，义为「摇摆的；不断改变方向的」

senses.title: To change direction suddenly
senses.definition: to turn or move in a new direction, especially an unplanned one
senses.definitionCN: 转向或朝新方向移动，尤指意料之外的转向
senses.example: The ball veered sharply to the right.
senses.exampleCN: 球突然向右急转。
senses.why: The core picture is a moving body leaving its straight line, so the first meaning is simply a change of direction while in motion.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是一个运动中的物体离开直线，所以第一层意思就是行进中改变方向，简单直接。

senses.title: To turn from a course or plan
senses.definition: to move away from an intended route or from a fixed course
senses.definitionCN: 偏离预定路线或偏离既定航向
senses.example: The plane veered off its planned flight path.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机偏离了原定航线。
senses.why: Once direction matters, a veer carries the idea of leaving a set line and heading somewhere else.
senses.whyCN: 一旦涉及方向，veer 就带有「离开既定路线、另走一边」的意味，因此自然表示脱离原定轨迹。

senses.title: To change position or opinion
senses.definition: to move or shift from one position, opinion, or course of action to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个立场、看法或做法转向另一个
senses.example: The discussion veered away from the main issue.
senses.exampleCN: 讨论慢慢偏离了主要议题。
senses.why: Direction becomes a metaphor for a line of argument, so a veer is a shift of stance rather than a physical turn.
senses.whyCN: 方向被借用来比喻论点的走向，所以 veer 从身体转向变成了立场转变。

senses.title: Of the wind, to turn clockwise
senses.definition: of the wind, to turn in a clockwise direction, or to change direction
senses.definitionCN: 指风顺时针转向，或改变风向
senses.example: The wind veered to the north and the sky cleared.
senses.exampleCN: 风转向北，天空放晴了。
senses.why: Sailors used veer for wind shifting round the compass, so the word entered the language through the weather.
senses.whyCN: 水手用 veer 指风围着罗盘转向，这个词正是从海上天气用语进入日常英语的。

senses.title: To turn a rope or vessel
senses.definition: to let out a rope or cable gradually, or to turn a ship
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐放出绳索缆绳，或转动船身
senses.example: The crew veered the line slowly as the boat drifted.
senses.exampleCN: 船漂流时，船员缓缓放出缆绳。
senses.why: Nautical use keeps the picture of a line being sent off in a different direction, the oldest part of the word.
senses.whyCN: 航海用法保留了「把绳索朝另一个方向送去」的画面，这是这个词最古老的一层含义。

intro.en: Veer is usually traced to Middle French virer, to turn, probably from a Romance verb of turning that has no certain Latin source. It entered English in the sixteenth century first as a nautical term.
intro.cn: veer 一般认为来自中古法语 virer（转动），其更早的来源不确定。它在十六世纪进入英语，最初是航海用语。

items.en: A turning verb of uncertain origin, probably from Vulgar Latin, lies behind virer.
items.cn: virer 背后是一个来源不确定的「转动」动词，一般认为来自通俗拉丁语。

items.en: Virer means to turn or to change course.
items.cn: 中古法语 virer 意为转动、改变航向。

items.en: Sixteenth century sailors use veer for letting out a rope and for turning a ship.
items.cn: 十六世纪的水手用 veer 表示放绳和转船。

items.en: The word also describes the wind turning clockwise round the compass.
items.cn: 这个词也用来描述风向沿罗盘顺时针转变。

items.en: Modern English extends veer to roads, arguments, prices, and opinions.
items.cn: 现代英语把 veer 扩展到道路、争论、价格与观点上。

note.en: Veer is often confused with veal and mere, and it sits close to swerve, veer is the gentler, more literary turn.
note.cn: veer 容易与 veal、mere 混淆；近义方面它与 swerve 最接近，但 veer 更缓和、更书面。

entries.definition: meat from a young calf
entries.definitionCN: 小牛肉（只是拼写相近，与转向无关）

entries.definition: nothing more than
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅的（只是押韵相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: changing direction
to change direction suddenly, especially to avoid hitting something
entries.definitionCN: 突然转向，尤指为躲避而急转

entries.definition: to move in a new direction
entries.definitionCN: 转动；转向（最普通的说法）

entries.definition: to depart from an established course

normalIntro.en: Veer is a short verb of turning: a straight line that suddenly bends, usually with the wind or the sea in the background.
normalIntro.cn: veer 是一个表示「转动」的短动词：笔直的线忽然弯开，背景里常常是风或海。

normal.en: The French source virer means to turn, and English took it first from sailors.
normal.cn: 法语来源 virer 意为转动，英语最早是从水手那里借来的。

normal.en: Veer off means to leave the road or the topic you were on.
normal.cn: veer off 表示偏离原来的道路或话题。

normal.en: In weather talk, the wind veers when it turns clockwise, while it backs when it turns the other way.
normal.cn: 在天气用语中，风顺时针转叫 veer，逆时针转则叫 back。

normal.en: Compare swerve: swerve is an urgent swerve to avoid a crash, veer can be slow and gentle.
normal.cn: 对比「swerve」：swerve 是为避撞而急打方向，veer 可以缓慢而轻柔。

normal.en: The noun veering and the adjective unveering come from the same verb.
normal.cn: 名词 veering 与形容词 unveering 都由这个动词而来。

abstract.en: Picture a car drifting slowly toward the edge of its lane, then pulling back.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车慢慢滑向车道边缘，然后又拉回来。

abstract.en: See a debate that starts on prices and ends up talking about the weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一场辩论从价格开始，最后却聊到了天气。

abstract.en: Imagine a weather vane swinging round as the wind shifts.
abstract.cn: 想象风向标随着风向改变而缓缓转动。

examples.en: The cyclist veered around the pothole and nearly hit the kerb.
examples.cn: 骑车人绕开坑洞急转，差点撞上路缘。

examples.en: Her talk veered between humour and serious warning.
examples.cn: 她的演讲在幽默与严肃警告之间来回转换。

examples.en: As the storm passed, the wind veered and the sailors changed course.
examples.cn: 风暴过后风向转变，水手们于是改了航向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威尔」——方向盘一打，车子就转向了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自中古法语 virer（转动），更早的罗曼语来源不确定 → 十六世纪英语 veer，核心义「转动、改变方向」；航海用语是它的起点。

sensesIntro.en: Veer starts as a physical turn, then becomes a turn off a set course, a shift of opinion, the clockwise turn of the wind, and a nautical handling of ropes.
sensesIntro.cn: veer 起初是身体上的转向，随后表示偏离既定路线、立场的转变、风向的顺时针改变，以及航海中的放绳转船。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line that bends away to one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条笔直的线忽然向一侧弯开。

branches.en: A moving body changes direction without warning.
branches.cn: 运动中的物体毫无预警地改变方向。

branches.en: Leaving a fixed route is the course sense.
branches.cn: 离开固定路线是「偏离」义项。

branches.en: A line of argument is a road, so opinions can veer too.
branches.cn: 论点像一条路，所以观点也会「转向」。

branches.en: Both wind and rope are physical examples of turning.
branches.cn: 风与绳索都是「转动」的具体例子。

branches.en: Every sense shares the jump from a set line to a new one.
branches.cn: 每个义项都共享同一个跳跃：从既定直线跳到新的方向。

intro.en: Veer is a simple one syllable verb with no productive English prefix; its family grows through common endings such as -ing and un-.
intro.cn: veer 是一个单音节简单动词，没有能产的英语前缀；它的词族靠 -ing、un- 这类常见词尾生长。

latinIntro.en: No Latin verb is securely behind veer; its nearest ancestry is Old French virer, so no Latin siblings are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: veer 背后没有可确认的拉丁语动词，最近的来源是古法语 virer，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Veer is the short base verb.
items.exampleCN: veer 是简短的动词原形。

items.example: The suffix -s gives veers.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 给出 veers。

items.example: The suffix -ed gives veered.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 给出 veered。

items.example: The suffix -ing gives veering.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 给出 veering。

items.example: Veering can also act as a noun.
items.exampleCN: veering 也可以作名词使用。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unveering.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unveering。

items.example: Unveering describes a steady course.
items.exampleCN: unveering 形容稳定的路线。

items.example: The particle off forms veer off.
items.exampleCN: 小品词 off 构成 veer off。
